jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Advancement Services
jobs.description:
GiveCampus is the world's leading fundraising platform for non-profit educational institutions. Trusted by millions of donors and 1,300+ colleges, universities, and K-12 schools, our mission is to help advance the quality, the affordability, and the accessibility of education. At our current pace, we will facilitate $100 billion in charitable giving over the next decade–enough money to send more than 1 million students to college, tuition-free.

GiveCampus is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, but we're also practitioners of Sustainable Growth: we've made the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies each of the last five years and we've been profitable nine of the last 10. In 2025, we celebrated a $140 million growth investment that included a major liquidity event for GiveCampus employees–the second in less than three years.

Our purpose-driven team of 130+ is located in 30+ states across the US: team members work from anywhere they choose. We have a beautiful 12,000sf office in Washington, DC that is available for people to use whenever they want, and we regularly organize team meet-ups, visit partner institutions, and host retreats in various locations.

While we operate at meaningful scale, we're still small relative to the commercial and social good opportunities in front of us. Every GiveCampus employee plays a meaningful role in shaping what comes next, and we're growing the team in support of our ambitious plans–including a $100 million investment in AI product development. If you believe in the transformative power of education and want to join a fast-growing, mission-driven company, you'll fit right in.

Location: This is a remote-first role based in the U.S. While we embrace flexible, distributed work, we also value in-person connection. Team members are expected to attend multiple company-wide and team-specific onsites throughout the year.
About the role

Everything GiveCampus is building runs on school data, and today, getting that data connected is the top reason a school's launch stalls. GC Intelligence, our AI that predicts which donors are likely to give and drafts outreach to them, needs a school's full donor history to work. So do Smart Ask Amounts, which suggest how much to ask each donor for, and GC Gift Officer, the tool fundraisers use to manage their donor relationships.

All of it depends on data flowing between GiveCampus and the school's CRM, where its advancement office (the fundraising and alumni relations team) keeps every donor, gift, and interaction. Only a fraction of our Partner schools send us their complete data. Closing that gap is one of the biggest growth levers in front of the company.

The Advancement Services team owns that flow. It's named for the advancement services staff at each school, the people who manage donor data and the main users of what we build. We connect GiveCampus to the CRMs schools run, mainly Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT and Salesforce-based systems such as Ascend and Affinaquest. We also own the API that schools and software partners use to send and pull data, the guided data importer that lets schools upload files of donor and gift records, and a new queue-driven pipeline on AWS designed to move tens of millions of records.

We're hiring two Senior Software Engineers to build that pipeline and the bidirectional integrations that run on it. A redelivered message can become a duplicate gift in a school's books, and the CRM on the other end may cap you at about 10 requests per second. You'll design for both. You'll also help set how the team builds with AI agents, from the checks and context files that keep agents on track to the guardrails that keep them away from donor data they shouldn't touch.

The team is small and the surface area is large, so you'll own big pieces of it from your first month. The code you ship decides whether a gift made on a giving day (a school's one-day fundraising push) lands in a school's CRM correctly that same day.

You'll work closely with the Advancement Services Product Manager, Partner Success, Partner Operations, and Data Science, plus the CRM vendors and connector partners whose APIs we build against. The team runs one-week sprints and ships to production multiple times a day.

We're hiring at two levels. At IC4, you'll own major components of the pipeline and integrations, with design input from the team. At IC5, you'll own the architecture of a system end to end, guide the team's agentic engineering practices, and mentor others through the work. If you're not sure which fits, apply and we'll figure it out together.

Successful outcomes

- A pipeline that holds up at scale. You design and ship AWS-based pipelines with idempotent consumers. You keep memory and database load bounded, throttling writes, budgeting connections, and keeping pipeline storage off the app database.

- Incremental syncs that stay correct. Runs pick up only what changed, using row hashing that holds up when batches run in parallel. You reconcile records that arrive from file uploads, the API, Raiser's Edge NXT, and the GiveCampus app, including deletes, and you handle rate limiting so no single job burns through a CRM's request budget.

- Migrations with a fallback. You move schools onto new infrastructure by proving parity with the old system first, then cutting over with the old path ready. Everything ships as infrastructure as code, with deploy, recovery, replay, and monitoring included from the start.

- No silent failures. Every sync reports to Sentry and New Relic, so the team sees a broken sync before a school's advancement services director does.

- A partner API developers want to build on. You design versioned, documented endpoints that go through a beta period before general availability, so the consultants and software partners who build integrations for schools can plan around them.

- An agentic practice the whole team uses. You write and maintain the context agents read and build reviewed skills for repeated work like stacked PRs and support-ticket triage. You measure whether a tooling change helped and you teach what works to the rest of the team.
What we're looking for

Required

- Pipelines at real volume. 6+ years building and running production backend systems, including a distributed ETL or sync pipeline that moved tens of millions of records. You can explain how your consumers handled redelivery, backpressure, and replay.

- Third-party integration scar tissue. You've built against APIs you didn't control and handled auth, token expiry in the middle of long pagination, rate limits, retries, and upsert semantics. You know what breaks when the other system changes without warning.

- Careful data modeling. You think in external IDs, timezone-safe bulk writes, and safe schema changes to busy core tables. Data integrity matters to you because someone on the other end reconciles every record.

- Clear, written communication. You write design docs and PR descriptions that a distributed team can act on without a meeting, and you're comfortable explaining a sync failure to a school's IT staff.

Strongly preferred

- AI-native, with receipts. You've made coding agents more reliable for a team by writing context files, building skills, or adding checks and evals. You can tell us about a time you didn't trust an agent's output and the check you added afterward.

- Infrastructure you can operate. You ship on AWS (or an equivalent cloud) with infrastructure as code, and you've owned the deploy, monitoring, and on-call side of what you built.
Bonus points

- Experience integrating with fundraising or nonprofit CRMs: Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT or its SKY API, Salesforce (including Ascend or Affinaquest), or school systems like Ellucian, Veracross, or Slate.

- Experience with Ruby on Rails and RSpec.

- You've built a public or partner-facing API product with OpenAPI documentation.

- You've worked in higher education advancement, nonprofit fundraising, or a nearby domain.
What you'll learn here

You don't need to know advancement data on day one. In your first 90 days, you'll learn Raiser's Edge NXT, the Blackbaud SKY API, and the Salesforce products we support. You'll also learn the building blocks of school fundraising data:

- Constituents: anyone a school tracks, such as alumni, parents, and donors.

- Hard and soft credits: who gave a gift, and who else gets recognized for it, like a spouse or a company that matched it.

- Recurring gifts and designations: gifts that repeat on a schedule, and the fund each gift goes to, such as financial aid or athletics.

- Opportunities and assignments: large gifts a fundraiser is working toward, and which fundraiser owns each donor relationship.

- Events: reunions, galas, and other gatherings, along with who registered and attended.

You'll get to know our pipeline codebase and our tools (Metabase for reporting, New Relic, and the Rails console). If you come from another backend framework, you'll pick up Rails along the way.

Our stack

- Ruby on Rails and React

- Postgres and Redis

- AWS, including SQS, Aurora, S3, and EKS

- REST APIs documented with OpenAPI, plus the Blackbaud SKY API, Salesforce, and other CRM APIs

- Sentry and New Relic for observability

- AI coding agents across the workflow, with shared context files, skills, and evals
How the team works

- You go deep on the other system's quirks. You'd rather read the SKY API changelog than guess at why a sync broke, and you want to know how a system got the way it is.

- You use AI agents by default and verify what they produce. You've built the checks that catch when they're wrong.

- You write it down. Design docs, PR descriptions, and incident notes that let a distributed team act without a meeting.

- Strong opinions, loosely held. You argue hard for your approach, then commit fully once the team decides.

- You care about the people on the other end: the advancement services staff reconciling every record, the fundraisers relying on the data, and the donors behind it all.

Keep an eye on your spam and promotions folders in case our emails end up there.

jobs.title: Software Engineer III — Evaluation
jobs.description:
GENERAL OVERVIEW:

Education Advanced, Inc. is a rapidly growing educational technology (Ed-Tech) company in the K-12 industry. Our goal is to create operational software that empowers educators to work more efficiently in specific areas.

Evaluation is our teacher and staff observation and evaluation product. It is a Ruby on Rails application hosted on AWS, and it includes AI-powered features that help educators do their best work. We are hiring a Software Engineer III to own significant parts of the product. This is a small, tight-knit team, so the role carries real breadth: you will work across the Rails application, our AI-powered features, the data integrations that connect Evaluation to other systems, and the cloud infrastructure it all runs on. You will also help others understand how the system works, so documentation and mentoring are part of the job, not something you get to after the sprint. You will start with a structured onboarding period, then help shape where the product and its architecture go next. This is a remote role with core availability during US Central Time business hours.

We foster a supportive, inclusive, and innovation-driven culture where every voice matters and your work directly empowers teachers and students. Join us to grow, collaborate, and build solutions that transform K–12 education.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Roles and Responsibilities

- Design, build, ship, and support features across the Evaluation application, from the first product conversation through release and production support.

- Build and improve AI-powered product features: integrate large language models (LLMs) into real user workflows, and help design the prompts, safeguards, and quality checks that keep AI output accurate, safe, and useful for educators.

- Build and maintain data integrations between Evaluation and other systems, with a focus on reliability and data quality.

- Lead technical improvements on the roadmap, such as simplifying configuration, reducing technical debt, and modernizing parts of the application, and sequence that work so delivery keeps moving.

- Write clean, high-quality, testable, secure, and maintainable code, and help strengthen our automated testing practices.

- Build and operate in AWS using CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and troubleshoot production issues end to end across the application and infrastructure.

-  Meet FERPA, state student-privacy, and WCAG accessibility requirements as part of normal delivery.

- Use AI-assisted development tools as a core part of how you work (planning, coding, testing, code review, and documentation) while checking everything they produce and standing behind every line you ship.

- Help shape how the team uses AI in the development lifecycle, including shared conventions, reusable prompts and instructions, and guardrails for safe use.

- Partner with Product Management to refine requirements, take part in backlog refinement and sprint planning, and turn specifications into scalable, secure implementations.

- Mentor teammates through code review, pairing, and technical planning, and write clear documentation that helps others work confidently in the system.

- Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 5+ years building and operating production web applications, including recent, hands-on Ruby on Rails experience (Ruby, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS).

- Strong relational database skills (MySQL or similar): schema design, indexing, query performance, and safe migrations in a multi-tenant application.

- Hands-on experience writing automated tests in Rails (for example, RSpec) at the unit and integration level.

- Hands-on experience deploying, running, and debugging applications in AWS, including containers, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure as code.

- Solid grasp of secure web development (for example, OWASP Top 10, authentication and authorization, input validation, and secrets management).

- Daily, hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools in professional work (for example, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenAI Codex), beyond autocomplete to multi-step work such as building features, refactoring, writing tests, and exploring unfamiliar code.

- Skill at directing AI tools: giving clear specs and context, breaking work into small, checkable steps, and using tests and code review to catch output that is wrong, insecure, or made up.

- Sound judgment about AI and data safety, including what code and data should never be shared with an AI tool, especially student and educator data.

- A track record of owning ambiguous work end to end, from design through delivery and support, without needing it broken down for you.

- Comfort working productively in a mature codebase and improving it without stalling delivery.

- Excellent written and verbal communication for async, cross-time-zone teamwork, including explaining technical tradeoffs to non-engineers.

- Experience working in an Agile team (backlog refinement, sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives).

- Core availability during US Central Time business hours.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Enterprise AI is moving from pilots to production, and the constraint is no longer the model — it's the data. Agents are only as good as what they can sense, trust, and act on in the moment, and real-time, event-driven data is becoming the foundation every serious AI system runs on.

Solace is the leading real-time data platform for the enterprise AI era. Established enterprises worldwide — including RBC Capital Markets, Bosch, Heineken, PSA Singapore, United Airlines, Schwarz Group, and hundreds more — have built their business around Solace to enable intelligent, real-time experiences, modernize their application and integration landscape, and create seamless digital journeys for their customers, partners, and employees.

So, the next time you drive a car, order furniture online, fly in a plane, check your bank balance on your phone, your positive experience could be a direct result of our technology—and your hard work!

About the Role

Solace is building Solace Diskless Streaming for Apache Kafka® (SSK), by the creators of Nisshi. SSK builds on Nisshi Diskless Streaming for Apache Kafka®, an open-source project licensed under Apache-2.0. Both implement the Apache Kafka® protocol and separate compute from storage. Stateless Protocol Engines scale out by adding more, and data is stored in object storage rather than on local disks.

Other systems depend on this platform, so writes must remain correct under heavy concurrent load. The work covers wire protocols, storage engines, and the coordination problems that arise in keeping order and consistency across stateless engines. The team focuses on scale, security, latency, and robustness, and tunes for tail latency, throughput, and cost per byte; object storage sets its own floor on latency. You will own pieces of the data path end to end, working in Rust. Part of that work takes place in public, in the Nisshi repository.

What You’ll Do

- Design and build core data-path components: request handling and storage, for a system that must hold strict ordering guarantees under load.

- Implement and evolve Apache Kafka® wire-protocol handling: parsing, framing, versioning, and backward compatibility with Apache Kafka® client libraries.

- Build and harden storage engines: offset and sequence coordination, compaction, retention, and correctness under concurrent access.

- Diagnose difficult defects: races, consistency edge cases, and security or robustness issues that surface only under real concurrent load.

- Profile and tune throughput and latency against measured production numbers.

- Work with the open-source community on Nisshi: review, discuss, and contribute.

What You’ll Bring to the Role

One of the Following, at a Deep Level:

- Hands-on experience building a high-throughput, log-based streaming or messaging system, such as Apache Kafka® or a comparable platform: wire protocols, client/server compatibility, and the internals of a system that can’t lose data.

- Deep experience with a database’s internals: storage engine, write-ahead-log or commit-log design, replication and consensus, or query execution. Any flavor counts (relational, graph, document, or otherwise). If you’ve solved these problems inside a database, you understand the ones we’re solving.

Both Paths Also Need:

- Strong systems-programming fundamentals (Rust, C++, Go, or Java).

- A track record of owning hard technical problems end to end, from design through production.

- Comfort working remotely and asynchronously, across time zones.

Preferred:

- Production experience in Rust.

- Working knowledge of the Apache Kafka® protocol, client libraries, and ecosystem.

- Hands-on experience working on the internals of a system like Apache Kafka®, Redpanda, Pulsar, WarpStream, NATS JetStream, or Solace Event Broker.

- Experience running one of these systems at production scale.

- Experience with security hardening, fuzzing, or performance engineering of network services.

Why You’ll Love Working at Solace

At Solace, we’re all about smart people, meaningful work, and good vibes.

- Work with brilliance – Our team is packed with some of the sharpest minds in the industry.

- Balance matters – We believe work should fit into your life, not the other way around.

- Hybrid-first – Flexibility is built into how we work, so everyone feels included and empowered.

- Values-driven – We live and breathe our core values: craftsmanship, trust, courage, freedom, momentum, humility, and human experience.

- Growth mindset – Our training programs are designed to help you level up, fast.

- Customer Obsessed – We’re proud of our world-class customer lineup (we’re not shy about it).

- Keep it fun – We’re social, we keep things simple, and we know how to have a good time.

- Creative culture – We’ve got a great sense of humour and we make cool videos on topics like MITT and this (check them out!).

At Solace, we are committed to a fair, inclusive, and transparent recruitment process.

To help identify candidates whose qualifications best align with the role, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools during the initial stage of resume screening. These tools compare submitted resumes to the job description, focusing on education, experience, and skills.

Importantly, all decisions beyond this initial screening—including interviews and final hiring—are made by our human recruitment team. AI is never used to make final hiring decisions.

Let’s Talk

Not sure you meet every requirement? That’s okay — we’re more interested in your potential and passion. If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you.

Need accommodations during the hiring process? Just let us know — we’re here to support you.

Thanks to everyone who applies! While we wish we could connect with every candidate, only those selected to move forward will be contacted.

At Solace, we believe that diversity and inclusion drive innovation and growth, both in business and in life. We strive to create an enriching and safe workplace where you can be who you are. If you want to do the best work of your career and feel supported every step of the way, we encourage you to join us!

jobs.title: Software Engineer I
jobs.description:
Build What's Next in Aerospace

For nearly a century, Simmonds Precision has been helping shape the future of flight from our home in Vergennes, Vermont. Today, our technologies are trusted across hundreds of commercial and military aircraft platforms worldwide, helping aircraft operate safely, reliably, and efficiently.

At Simmonds Precision, we design and manufacture advanced sensing, monitoring, fuel management, and precision control technologies that solve some of aerospace's most demanding challenges. Behind every solution is a team of talented people who bring together engineering expertise, advanced manufacturing, craftsmanship, and a drive to innovate.

When you join Simmonds Precision, you're not just taking the next step in your career, you're contributing to technology that takes flight around the world. Whether your expertise is in engineering, manufacturing, quality, operations, or business support, there's an opportunity to make your mark.

Find your next opportunity where precision meets possibility—and build your career in aerospace with Simmonds Precision.

What You Will Do
As a Software Engineer, you will leverage cutting-edge development workflows to build the precise, intelligent, and secure software powering tomorrow's Monitoring and Actuation Systems. While ensuring the reliability of our existing production software, you will actively innovate—engineering next-generation, mission-critical solutions trusted in the world's most demanding environments.
Your focus will center on two core product lines:

- Health Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): Empowering aircraft operators to analyze fleet conditions, predict emerging mechanical anomalies early, and optimize maintenance schedules with high accuracy and confidence.

- Aircraft Actuation Systems: Transforming control inputs into deterministic, high-precision movement across flight control surfaces. You will support varied rotary/linear architectures, AC/DC power frameworks, and fly-by-wire system compliance.
You will join our Next Generation Engineering Team—a collaborative unit of innovators and aviation enthusiasts redefining modern HUMS and actuation technologies. We balance deep technical rigor with a dynamic, fast-iterating startup energy. This is an environment built for hands-on experimentation with cutting-edge tools to shape the future.
What You Will Learn

- Develop and optimize embedded flight-software for safety-critical systems used in commercial aircraft and military platforms.

- Write high-performance, deterministic code and conduct debugging and validation using simulation tools.

- Collaborate closely with systems engineers, hardware teams to deliver integrated solutions that meet stringent aviation safety, performance, and certification requirements.

- Implement and support AI-assisted onboard features.

- Conduct debugging and validation using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, hardware debuggers, simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) environments.

- Ensure compliance with aviation safety standards such as DO-178, and adherence to secure coding and cyber-resilience practices.

- Participate in flight-test operations, lab testing, and simulation runs to evaluate system performance under real-world and mission-critical conditions.
Qualifications You Must Have

- Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) major obtained by start date.

- Experience may be obtained through on-the-job experience, research, coursework, or projects.
Qualifications We Prefer

- Prior internship, co-op, or work experience.

- An emphasis on strong collaboration and communication skills, with a desire to achieve world class abilities to work within dynamic teams to solve challenging problems.

- Basic understanding of aircraft operational fundamentals is highly desirable, as the role involves executing flight test scenarios to validate system functionality and performance. This hands-on work will enable the candidate to directly contribute to the advancement of next-generation aerospace technologies.
Why Join Simmonds Precision?

At Simmonds Precision, you won't just be filling a position, you'll be developing skills in an industry where precision matters. You'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, gain hands-on manufacturing experience, and contribute to products used in demanding aerospace applications.

Compensation & Benefits

Great work deserves great rewards—and benefits that support you both at work and beyond. Our comprehensive total rewards package is designed to help you stay healthy, build financial security, enjoy time away from work, and continue growing throughout your career.

- Health & Wellness: Take care of yourself and your family with comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, HSA and FSA options, and convenient access to an onsite cafeteria and fitness center.

- Invest in Your Future: Enjoy competitive pay, an annual bonus opportunity, and a 401(k)-retirement plan that includes up to a 4% company match plus an additional annual employer contribution starting at 3%. Company-paid life and disability insurance provide additional financial protection and peace of mind.

- Time to Recharge: We believe time away from work matters. Enjoy four weeks of vacation, plus five additional paid days during our annual holiday shutdown, paid sick leave, and paid maternity and paternity leave—giving you more time for the moments that matter.

- Grow Your Career: Keep building your skills and advancing your career with up to $20,000 in annual tuition reimbursement, along with ongoing professional development and learning opportunities.

- Benefits Beyond the Basics: Choose from additional programs designed to make life a little easier, including supplemental insurance, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), legal services, identity theft protection, discounted auto and home insurance, and pet insurance.

Your career is more than a paycheck. Join a company that invests in your health, your future, your growth, and your life outside of work.

Shift: First Shift

Compensation: $57,200-108,800/year

jobs.title: Software Engineer, PowerClerk
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Looking for a job that makes a real difference in our world today and one that you’ll be proud of when you look back in 20, 30 or 40 years? This is it. Clean Power Research® is advancing the energy transformation through cloud software that informs, streamlines and values energy-related decisions and processes for utilities, energy professionals and consumers.

We’re a growing company that counts 10 of the top 10 Fortune 500 utilities and many of the largest renewable energy companies in the U.S. as our customers. We’re focused on expanding our market reach and impact with new software technologies that help solve the energy industry’s hardest problems.

At Clean Power Research, every employee has a seat at the table and an important role.

Why Work Here?

- Go from building solutions to being part of the solution

- Join a growing team of software and energy veterans from companies like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle, General Electric and Pacific Gas & Electric

- Bring your passion and ideas to the table

- Use your creativity to solve hard problems and make tough decisions

- Work in a start-up like environment coupled with the stability and customer base of an established, profitable company

- Realize work-life balance; we like to see our families, friends and pets at night!

- Join a growing company that expects you to grow with us and invests in your growth

Clean Power Research offers competitive compensation and benefits to full-time employees including medical/dental/vision, paid vacation, paid holidays, a bonus plan and 401(k) plan with matching.

What You’ll Be Doing as a Software Engineer

Our Engineering Team develops Software-as-a-Service (Saas) solutions hosted in the cloud using sophisticated development tools and cutting-edge cloud infrastructure. As a software engineer, you’ll be learning and contributing to the development of highly scalable, reliable, performant and secure software products.

One of the interesting and fun challenge you’ll face here is:

Energy resource workflow automation

On the PowerClerk® team, you’ll work on the leading software service for utility program automation. PowerClerk powers the rollout and adoption of distributed energy resources (e.g., solar, batteries/storage and electric vehicles) at some of the largest utilities in the U.S. by digitizing utility programs through intuitive, self-service interfaces that enable extensive process automation as well as utility back-end system integration. You’ll be writing code used by hundreds of thousands of utility employees, utility customers and energy industry professionals that helps these energy technologies get installed and have an impact.

This is a full-stack position where you’ll design, build, and own features end-to-end. You’ll be using C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, JavaScript frameworks and SQL in a cloud-hosted (AWS) environment. You’ll be part of an agile, empowered and high-performing team. You’ll have exposure to customers and the business, and be an important participant in product, design and technology decisions.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Deliver high-quality code and features with a high-degree of ownership

- Participate in writing test automation (unit tests and integration tests) and be part of a combined engineering team

- Collaborate with other team members to define the product and make it great

- Participate in release testing, monitoring of performance and functionality of the service in production

- Effectively use modern AI-assisted development tools to support software development activities including writing and understanding code, troubleshooting issues, developing tests, and improving developer productivity

Who You Are

- 1+ years of professional software development experience

- Someone who has strong aptitude for problem solving and consistently delivers high quality code

- BA/BS or MS degree in Computer Science or related technical discipline

- Experience in building web applications/services using C#/ASP.NET/SQL and running in a cloud-hosted environment is a plus

- Some experience with AI-assisted development tools and a strong interest and willingness to learn, adopt, and become proficient with AI tools as part of the software development process

- Passion for renewables and for advancing the energy transition to clean energy
Pay Range and Benefits

- Base Salary Range: $90,000 to $110,000 annual depending on experience

- Benefits: Performance-Based Bonus, Company Equity Plan

- Benefits: Paid Time Off, Sick Time, Holidays, Medical/Dental/Vision/Life and Disability Insurance, 401(k), Parental Leave, Commuter Benefits
How To Apply

Click the link below to submit your resume. Please include a cover letter detailing your interest in this position and the renewable energy space along with your resume. Due to the large number of applicants for our positions, we regret that we can only respond to candidates who meet our requirements.

Clean Power Research is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

The company’s employment decisions are based on merit, competence, performance and business needs.

Points North is looking for a Software Engineer in Test who is excited about doing meaningful, high-impact work on a product that people already depend on and making it better. You will be joining a small, fast-moving Agile team with the specific mission of modernizing the quality practices around a mature production application. You will be working with systems that real people use every day to do their job, and you are excited to make things measurably better than you found them.

If you are the kind of Engineer who gets energized by bringing structure and confidence to a complex codebase, who sees a legacy system as an opportunity rather than a liability, and who wants to build the testing foundation that carries a product into its next era we want to talk to you.

What You'll Be Doing:
- 
Enable the QA modernization journey. Partner with software engineers, other quality engineers, and product managers to assess where the application stands today and chart a practical path toward modern, sustainable quality practices without over-engineering the solution.
- 
Balance manual and automated testing. Apply targeted manual testing where it delivers the most insight while systematically expanding automated coverage over time. Know when each approach is the right tool for the job.
- 
Design, develop, and maintain automated test suites for our SaaS products using Playwright, C# and TypeScript, including end-to-end (E2E), integration, and API tests.
- 
Build test tools, frameworks, and utilities that improve coverage, accelerate execution, and make the whole team more effective.
- 
Leverage AI tools as a force multiplier, not a shortcut. Use AI thoughtfully to expand test coverage, accelerate test creation and maintenance, and surface insights.
- 
Participate in code reviews, pair programming, and agile events as a core member of the team.
- 
Help define and evolve testing strategies and best practices across the team as the codebase and product mature.
- 
Follow DevSecOps best practices for CI/CD and contribute to deployment automation.
- 
Continuously learn and grow technically, collaboratively, and in how you think about quality.
What We Are Looking For:
- 
A hands-on QA engineer with a developer mindset who is genuinely excited about legacy modernization. We are looking for someone who sees complexity as a puzzle worth solving.
- 
A practical thinker who balances automated coverage with targeted manual testing, and knows that the goal is confidence, not coverage numbers.
- 
Someone who is enthusiastic about AI as an enabler. Someone who is eager to experiment with AI-assisted tooling to move faster and reach further, while understanding that AI augments good engineering judgment rather than replacing it.
- 
A collaborator who communicates openly, takes pride in their work and their team's work, and leaves codebases and processes better than they found them.
- 
A builder who wants to see their work ship, make an impact, and solve real world problems.
Qualifications:
- 
5+ years of experience in professional software development or software quality engineering.
- 
Proven, professional experience building and utilizing test automation tools and frameworks.
- 
Proficiency with languages such as C# and/or TypeScript.
- 
Experience testing REST APIs and using tools like Postman or equivalent automation frameworks.
- 
Experience with source control and modern CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions).
- 
Comfortable working with relational databases such as SQL Server.
- 
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work as a core member of an Agile software development team.
- 
Solid understanding of modern software engineering principles and best practices.
- 
Experience working in a SaaS company or small, fast-paced development team.
- 
Familiarity with cloud services (Azure App Services, Azure SQL, Azure Functions).
- 
Experience bringing QA practices to legacy or established codebases.

At Points North, we believe that taking care of our team is the foundation of our success. That’s why we’ve created a benefits package designed to support you both personally and professionally:
- 
Health Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans are available to keep you and your family healthy.
- 
Retirement Savings: Invest in your future with employer-matching contributions to a SIMPLE Traditional and/or ROTH IRA plan.
- 
Time Off: Generous PTO, paid holidays, and Volunteer Time Off (VTO) are offered so that you can take time to recharge and give back to what matters to you.
- 
Growth Opportunities: Professional development is encouraged whether it be in training, certifications, or other opportunities to boost your career.
- 
Flexibility: Depending on the role, remote or hybrid arrangements may be made available to fit your lifestyle and business needs.
For this position the base salary range is $110,000 - $125,000 per year, plus annual bonus eligibility. Final compensation determinations will reflect your unique experience, skills, and the responsibilities of the role.
At Points North, you’ll find an energizing, ambitious and supportive workplace where your contributions make a real impact. Ready to join our team? Apply today to take the next step in your career!

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer (Full-Stack, AI-Native)
Marvin · Denver/Los Angeles - Hybrid 2-day in office · Full-time · $160k-190k
About Marvin
Marvin helps people navigate their mental health and wellbeing. We partner with employers and health plans to give their members one place to understand their coverage, find care, and get support, including an AI coach built into the product. We're a small team shipping a production healthcare application, which means every engineer touches things that matter and owns them end to end.
The role
We're hiring a senior full-stack engineer who has made AI a core part of how they build software, not a novelty. This is not a machine learning research role. You won't train models or tune GPUs. You will ship product in a modern TypeScript/Next.js stack, and you'll do it with AI woven into both the product and your own workflow.
Two things distinguish this role from a standard senior web position:
- 
You build with AI. You've moved well past autocomplete. You direct agentic coding tools to do real, multi-step work, you know exactly where they break, and you own every line they produce.
- 
You build AI into the product. You've shipped LLM-backed features to real users and lived with them in production: prompts, tool calls, evals, tracing, cost, latency, and failure modes.
What you'll do
- 
Own features end to end across our Next.js/React/TypeScript app, Prisma/Postgres backend, and AWS infrastructure.
- 
Extend our AI coach and build new LLM-powered member experiences: retrieval over benefits data, structured extraction, guided flows, and agentic tool use against our own APIs.
- 
Design evaluation and observability for AI features so we know when they get worse, not just when they crash.
- 
Push our AI-assisted development practice forward: agent instructions, reusable skills, hooks, MCP integrations, and review practices that keep quality high as velocity climbs.
- 
Handle sensitive health data responsibly. PHI boundaries, redaction, audit trails, and vendor data agreements are part of the design, not an afterthought.
- 
Review code, whether written by a human or an agent, with a critical eye. Mentor teammates and raise the bar on testing and reliability.
What we're looking for
Core engineering
- 
5+ years building production web applications, with deep TypeScript, React, and Node experience. Next.js is a strong plus.
- 
Comfort across the stack: relational data modeling (we use Prisma and Postgres), auth flows, caching, background jobs, and cloud deployment (AWS, Docker, Terraform or similar).
- 
A real testing habit at every layer: unit, component, and end-to-end. We use Vitest, Storybook, Cypress, and Playwright.
- 
Strong product judgment and the ability to work directly with design, clinical, and partner-facing teammates.
AI fluency (the part that sets you apart)
- 
Daily, expert use of agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. You write project instructions and reusable skills for your agents, hand them multi-step tasks, and review the output like a senior reviewer, not a rubber stamp.
- 
Hands-on experience shipping LLM features: prompt design and versioning, structured outputs, tool/function calling, streaming UIs, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-turn conversation state.
- 
You've run evals and traced production LLM traffic (LangSmith, Braintrust, Langfuse, or homegrown), and you can explain what changed the last time a model version bumped underneath you.
- 
You understand the cost, latency, and quality triangle and have made real trade-offs: model selection, caching, prompt compression, and fallback strategies.
- 
Clear-eyed about limits. You know when an LLM is the wrong tool, how to constrain one when it's the right tool, and how to keep a hallucination from ever reaching a member.
Nice to have
- 
Healthcare, benefits, or other regulated-data experience (HIPAA, SOC 2).
- 
Building MCP servers or internal agent tooling for a team.
- 
Experience with Clerk, Stripe, or Sentry.
- 
Contributions to AI developer tooling, open source or internal.
How we work
AI is part of our engineering culture, not a side experiment. Our repository ships with agent configuration, we maintain shared skills for code review and security checks, and we expect engineers to spend more of their time on judgment and less on typing. We also expect the opposite discipline: no unreviewed AI-generated code lands, and "the agent wrote it" is never an explanation for a bug.
Compensation and benefits
160-190k base salary · Equity · Health, dental, and vision · [401(k)] · Unlimited PTO · Hybrid 2 days/wk in office (LA or Denver)
Marvin is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
Compensation Range: $160K - $190K

jobs.description:
L'opportunité

Nous recherchons un(e) développeur(se) logiciel sénior, établi(e) à Montréal, au Canada, ou travaillant à distance dans le fuseau horaire de la côte Est des États-Unis, pour se joindre à une nouvelle équipe de développement chargée d’assurer la prise en charge de la plateforme Unity pour un écosystème Android englobant les appareils mobiles, les ordinateurs portables et les appareils hybrides. L’objectif principal de cette équipe est de permettre aux développeur(se)s Unity de déployer leurs titres de façon fluide sur ces appareils, tout en tirant pleinement parti de leurs capacités matérielles et logicielles uniques, notamment l’utilisation optimisée de l’affichage, l’intégration native des périphériques d’entrée et les services propres à chaque plateforme.

L’équipe sera également chargée de rechercher et de mettre en œuvre des optimisations de l’environnement d’exécution afin d’améliorer les performances de démarrage et l’efficacité d’exécution sur les appareils d’entrée de gamme comme sur les appareils haute performance. Pour ce faire, elle établira des points de référence en matière de performance, collaborera avec des expert(e)s internes et externes du domaine afin de mener des analyses rigoureuses des performances du moteur Unity sur la plateforme, et travaillera avec les principales parties prenantes à la mise en œuvre d’améliorations validées.

Les candidat(e)s doivent posséder une expertise en C++, en C# et en programmation de systèmes Android, ainsi qu’une expérience démontrée dans la création de logiciels de grande qualité à grande échelle.

Ce que vous ferez
- 
Travailler au sein d’une équipe agile afin de concevoir et de développer des fonctionnalités et des Workflow dans l’éditeur Unity qui prennent en charge ces configurations de plateforme particulières.

Évaluer, analyser et repérer les possibilités d’optimisation dans l’ensemble de la pile technologique, puis collaborer avec plusieurs équipes afin de développer des solutions.
- 
Rédiger une documentation technique complète et participer activement aux processus de révision de la conception.
- 
Assurer la stabilité de la plateforme en examinant et en résolvant les signalements de bogues.
- 
Renforcer la qualité et la livraison grâce aux tests automatisés et à des révisions de code rigoureuses, tout en favorisant une culture d’innovation, de collaboration et d’excellence technique.

Ce que nous recherchons
- 
Une solide expérience de la programmation de systèmes Android, appuyée par une maîtrise avancée de C++, de C# et de Java ou Kotlin.
- 
Une expérience de la création et de la maintenance de systèmes de plateforme ou d’environnements d’exécution.
- 
Une solide compréhension de la façon dont les applications de grande envergure utilisent plusieurs langages, notamment de l’exécution des appels synchrones et asynchrones, ainsi que de la gestion, de la propriété et du transfert de la mémoire entre ces langages.
- 
Une expérience de la conception et de la mise en œuvre d’ensembles de fonctionnalités évolutifs dans une base de code multithread de grande envergure.
- 
Des compétences en diagnostic, en débogage et en profilage des performances.

Vous avez peut-être également

Une compréhension approfondie de C# et des environnements d’exécution gérés.
- 
Une connaissance des méthodes de rendu 3D en temps réel et des API graphiques modernes, y compris Vulkan.

Une approche méthodique de la recherche et du développement de solutions d’optimisation novatrices.

Une passion pour l’avenir des jeux vidéo ou des expériences 3D en temps réel dans divers contextes.

Une connaissance des meilleurs moments et des meilleures façons d’utiliser l’intelligence artificielle dans le processus de développement logiciel.

The opportunity

We are seeking a Senior Software Developer, based either in Montreal, Canada or working remotely within the US East Coast time zone, to join a newly established development team responsible for delivering Unity platform support for an Android-based ecosystem encompassing mobile, laptop, and hybrid form factors. The primary objective of this team is to enable Unity developers to seamlessly deploy titles across these devices while fully leveraging their unique hardware and software capabilities, including optimized display utilization, native input integration, and platform-specific services.

The team is also charged with researching and implementing runtime optimizations to improve startup performance and execution efficiency across both entry-level and high-performance devices. This will be accomplished by establishing performance benchmarks, collaborating with internal and external domain experts to conduct rigorous performance analyses of the Unity engine on the platform, and partnering with key stakeholders to execute verified enhancements.

Certified as a Great Place to Work®, with 100% of employees saying they love working here, Rise8 is where bold ideas become real capabilities. Where mission meets meaning. And where fewer bad things happen because of bad software.
About You

- You're mission-driven and measure success by impact (lives saved, time returned, missions advanced), not activity.

- You think big, start small, and scale fast. You treat time as the biggest vulnerability and security as something that enables speed.

- You lead with kindness and candor: you give honest feedback, take it well, and raise the bar for everyone around you.

- You're an owner. You thrive with autonomy, act decisively, and stay steady when things are uncertain.

- You're building with AI and see it as a force multiplier not a shortcut.
As a Senior Software Engineer at Rise8, you will:

- Work with clients who may be new to modern software practices such as design thinking, AI-assisted and agentic engineering, continuous-release deployment, backlog management, or even interacting directly with the users they provide software to.

- Decompose business problems into clear, actionable instructions and specifications for agentic development.

- Be responsible for learning how your client likes to learn, how they like to receive feedback, and what ubiquitous language they use so you can speak in terms that resonate with them.

- Learn, teach, and refine your approach constantly to best collaborate towards a new way of thinking about engineering.

- On enablement engagements, pair with client developers, engineers, and military service members. Accelerate how they develop and deliver user stories that provide business value, technical feasibility, and user-driven functionality.

- Ensure that development is delivered week over week and continuously gauge feedback from real users in real time.

- Work with a balanced team in mind while building software that fits the user needs, business objectives, and stakeholder vision so the team can quickly make informed engineering decisions based on validated assumptions.

- Plan for and build delivery and user metrics into the software systems you create, so the team can measure real outcomes.

- Lead within your Rise8 product team by tracking and managing tech debt, facilitating engineering discussions, and leveling up less experienced engineers.
Qualifications

- Must have an active DoD security clearance.

- Must have working proficiency to advanced Palantir Foundry / Warp Core experience

- Strong communication skills and interest in a pair-programming environment.

- Experience leveraging AI in software development.

- Experience with Test Driven Development (TDD) and agile methodologies, including using AI tools to write and maintain tests.

- You have a strong understanding of algorithms, programming language theory, software architecture, networks, databases, and design patterns, and understand how to apply them.

- Experience with both frontend and backend.

- Experience using container technologies such as Docker or Kubernetes.

- Familiarity with DevSecOps tools and processes such as Git, Ansible, GitLabCI, SonarQube, Fortify, and ThreadFix.

- Demonstrated experience with API Development.

- You are comfortable running your software in Linux environments.

- You have strong facilitation skills.

- BA/BS in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience in training, mentoring and/or up-skilling engineers.

- Experience developing cloud-native applications.

- Experience leading a product or development team.

- Experience building and deploying in a continuous delivery environment.

- Experience working directly with clients.

- Experience with DoD, especially at a DoD "Software Factory".

- Preferred, not a requirement: located within a commutable distance into Colorado Springs, CO or El Segundo, CA
Travel

Position may require up to 25% travel in support of contract performance, customer site visits, and program activities.

Salary

The annual salary range for this role as it is posted is $143,824 to $179,780 regardless of final candidate location within the United States. The final job level and annual salary will be determined based on the education, qualification, knowledge, skills, ability, and experience of the final candidate(s), and calibrated against relevant market data and internal team equity.

Benefits

- Flexible schedule in a 100% distributed workforce

- Premium Insurance: We cover up to 100% of the employee premium and up to 80% of the combined dependent premium on our base health plan depending on pay band. We also cover 100% of the premium for employee and dependent Dental and Vision as well as employee premiums for Life and Disability coverage.

- Retirement: 401k match at 10% gross pay.

- Paid time off (PTO): 4 weeks combined accrued vacation and sick leave, 11 Federal holidays, your birthday, jury duty, and bereavement.

- Education & Training: Accrued budget of up to $4,000 per year for classes, travel, events, and materials.

- Wellness Budget: To encourage and support a well-rounded healthy lifestyle, we cover 50% reimbursement on a variety of wellness activities and products, up to $500 per calendar year.

- Equipment: We offer a MacBook Pro and multi-port adapter.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer / Technical Lead - Adobe CommerceIntegrations to help architect, evolve, and operate our enterprise e-commerce platform and its ecosystem of business-critical integrations.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role for an experienced engineer who excels at solving complex operational challenges, designing resilient integrations, enforcing modern engineering standards, and elevating the capabilities of an engineering team.

A primary focus of this role is leading backend architecture, performance optimization, and operational reliability on Adobe Commerce (Magento 2.4+), alongside designing the integration pipelines that connect our storefront directly to our enterprise systems. Our broader technology stack includes ERP, CRM, marketing automation, vendor networks, and external services connected through APIs. Our environment currently features Microsoft Dynamics GP, Magento, and HubSpot, with Dynamics GP planned to transition to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

The successful candidate does not need to be an expert in every individual tool across our enterprise. We are seeking someone with strong software engineering fundamentals, deep and proven Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 backend architecture experience, and a track record of building resilient integrations between transactional storefronts and core enterprise platforms. While our storefront runs on Adobe Commerce on Cloud (PaaS), we strongly welcome applications from master Magento 2 architects whose background is primarily in Microsoft Azure, AWS, Docker, or enterprise on-premise hosting. True Magento architectural mastery, clean module design, and systems integration expertise are what matter most; we will fully support your onboarding to Adobe Cloud-specific tooling.

This position combines active code contribution with technical leadership. You will remain hands-on in the codebase while shaping architecture, instituting automated testing and code-quality gates, guiding sprint delivery, and mentoring internal developers and external agency partners.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

Adobe CommercePlatform Engineering

- 
Lead backend architecture, module development, customization, and maintenance on Adobe Commerce (Magento 2.4+).
- 
Design clean, decoupled custom modules following Adobe best practices (dependency injection, plugins/interceptors, service contracts, declarative schema).
- 
Oversee platform deployment lifecycles, environment configurations, and build/deploy processes on Adobe Commerce Cloud.
- 
Configure, tune, and troubleshoot core platform infrastructure dependencies including Fastly / Varnish caching, Redis cache and session management, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, and RabbitMQ message brokers.
- 
Lead version upgrades, security patch implementations (Quality Patches Tool), and technical health audits to minimize technical debt and security vulnerabilities.
- 
Ensure optimal application performance, Core Web Vitals compliance, efficient indexing, and checkout transaction throughput.
- 
Enforce strict code governance across third-party marketplace extensions to prevent performance bottlenecks, security vulnerabilities, or upgrade conflicts.
- 
Collaborate with infrastructure teams to optimize platform hosting on Microsoft Azure, including media storage, networking, and cloud resource provisioning.

Systems IntegrationData Synchronization

- 
Architect, build, and support high-reliability integrations connecting Adobe Commerce with ERP (Microsoft Dynamics GP and Dynamics 365 Business Central), CRM, marketing automation (HubSpot), payment gateways, tax calculation engines, and fulfillment providers.
- 
Implement integration flows utilizing Adobe Commerce asynchronous and bulk APIs, REST/GraphQL endpoints, webhooks, and event-driven patterns.
- 
Design resilient integration pipelines with idempotency, robust queue processing, automated retries, failure reconciliation, and comprehensive audit trails.
- 
Establish centralized logging, application monitoring, and real-time alerting for storefront health and data-sync failures.
- 
Partner with ERP and martech teams to establish clear system-of-record boundaries and data governance rules across products, inventory, customer records, contract pricing, and orders.
- 
Leverage secure enterprise networking patterns (e.g., Azure Private Link, secure service bus/queues, and API gateways) to establish low-latency, private connectivity between Adobe Commerce and internal Microsoft Dynamics ERP services.

Technical LeadershipGovernance

- 
Provide hands-on technical leadership to a small-to-medium development team (including internal developers and specialized agency partners) while contributing directly to production code.
- 
Translate business and commercial requirements into scalable technical architectures, detailed implementation plans, and clear technical tickets.
- 
Conduct thorough, constructive code reviews and enforce strict engineering standards, PSR compliance, and Magento marketplace coding guidelines.
- 
Identify architectural bottlenecks, integration risks, and operational dependencies early in the project lifecycle.
- 
Mentor engineers, foster engineering best practices, and lead technical post-mortems for production or data synchronization incidents.

Agile DeliveryCollaboration

- 
Actively participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, estimation, daily stand-ups, and retrospectives.
- 
Collaborate closely with product managers, digital leadership, infrastructure teams, and vendor engineering groups to ensure alignment on milestones and technical feasibility.
- 
Translate intricate business logic into clear technical specs, acceptance criteria, and Definition of Done standards.
- 
Clearly articulate technical tradeoffs, risk assessments, and architectural decisions to technical peers and executive business stakeholders.

Quality, SecurityOperations

- 
Champion automated testing practices, including PHPUnit unit and integration tests, API verification, and operational health checks.
- 
Maintain structured, automated CI/CD pipelines supporting seamless branching, testing, staging, and zero-downtime production deployments.
- 
Ensure strict compliance with secure development standards, PCI-DSS requirements, role-based access control, input validation, and secure credential handling.
- 
Maintain comprehensive observability over platform transactions, API rate limits, and synchronization health using APM and log-management tools.

AI-Assisted Software Development

We view AI-assisted development tools as a valuable component of modern engineering workflows. We welcome engineers who responsibly leverage AI to improve productivity, code quality, and delivery speed.

Potential applications include:

- 
Accelerating boilerplate generation for modules, XML schema definitions ('di.xml', 'layout.xml'), and data patches.
- 
Generating unit and integration test coverage.
- 
Parsing and diagnosing complex error logs, deploy scripts, and stack traces.
- 
Accelerating documentation and code comprehension across large, inherited codebases.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Our client runs the compliant system of record you build on to move, store, and grow money. Launch financial products your customers love. We provide the financial primitives, licenses, and compliance, and our forward deployed team gets you live in two weeks. Under the hood, fiat and blockchain run as one system. Their customers never see any of it. Money comes in, money goes out, and it just gets there.The RoleYou'll be joining a lean, high-intensity engineering team at an inflection point, processing billions in volume today. You'll work directly with our CTO, contributing full-stack from week one.1. Building Infrastructure That Moves MoneyYou'll work on the core systems that power global payments. State machines, transaction pipelines, reconciliation flows. Accuracy is non-negotiable when money is on the line, but so is the ability to build systems that adapt as the financial landscape evolves. You'll own features end-to-end, think carefully about failure modes, and write code you're proud to put your name on.2. Shaping the ProductYou're not just implementing tickets. You'll collaborate closely with our CTO, BD team, and directly with customers to evolve our API and platform, making complex financial flows feel intuitive for the developers and businesses building on top of us. If you see a better way to build something, you'll say so. If a tradeoff matters, you'll surface it. We want engineers who think like owners.3. Setting the BarAs an early engineering hire, you'll have an outsized influence on how we build. The patterns we establish, the standards we hold, the culture we cultivate. We believe quality engineering lives at the intersection of theory and experimentation. Think rigorously, ship decisively. You'll help define what that looks like in practice.Who You AreYou're a strong individual contributor who works well across the full team. You don't need someone looking over your shoulder. You take ownership of your work end-to-end, communicate honestly about timelines and constraints, and never let something fall through the cracks because it wasn't technically "your problem."You're comfortable with the full stack.You have at least 4+ years shipping production-grade infrastructure with Node and NestJS (or something comparable) and React with TypeScript. You're proficient building client facing APIs and asynchronous backend systems with complex state machines (event queuing, job scheduling, webhook delivery, failure recovery, and so on). You move fluidly between frontend and backend depending on what the problem requires. You care about design and have high standards for what you ship. Not just whether it works, but whether it feels right.You're built for startups. You know what it means to operate in an environment with high ambiguity and real stakes. You move fast, make good decisions under uncertainty, and find energy in the challenge rather than frustration in the chaos. You've worked in a high-growth environment before, or you're deeply ready for one.You're obsessed with correctness and resilience. Moving money globally means the margin for error is low. You think carefully about edge cases, error handling, and what happens when things go wrong, because they will. You love a good state machine. You appreciate systems that are both robust and easy to reason about.You're curious about what we're building. You don't need to come from a fintech background, but you should be genuinely interested in stablecoins, global payments, and the financial infrastructure being rebuilt around them. The engineers who thrive here see the mission as part of the appeal, not just the tech stack.What Success Looks Like
- You're shipping meaningful features from week one, contributing to our platform and API with minimal ramp-up time
- The systems you build are reliable, readable, and maintainable, with code that the team is proud of and that scales with us
- You've raised the bar through the patterns you introduce, the reviews you give, and the standards you hold
- You've become a key voice on engineering decisions, someone our CTO relies on when it mattersLocation: NYC or DenverAbout Us: We're a recruiting, staffing, and placement company for Startups.Please submit your resume. If you're a good fit, we will connect you directly with our client who is hiring for this role.Work Location: In person

Please note: ONLY engineers currently living in Texas will be consideredWe are building a new billing platform from the ground up and need the senior engineer who owns its core: the engine that moves claims and payments through their lifecycles, the background job system that runs every automated step, and the integrations with payers, clearinghouses and banks. Backend engineering on a money system, TypeScript on PostgreSQL on Azure, working directly with the CTO on a team that stays at two to four engineers.The type of engineer we are seeking:A backend engineer who has shipped a transactional system (payments, claims, orders, ledgers, anything where a row posting twice is a real problem) in a typed language, and who has been the one who found out when it broke.Experience you must have:
- Seven or more years of backend engineering in production, in a typed language: TypeScript or Node.js, C#, Java, Go or Kotlin. TypeScript is what we use. A strong C# or Java engineer who has not written much TypeScript is fine; a Python-only engineer is not.
- A relational database as their primary store for years. PostgreSQL preferred; SQL Server, DB2, Oracle or MySQL fine. They should be able to talk about transactions, locking and a deadlock they debugged.
- Built and ran something with background workers, queues and retries. The tool does not matter (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS, Azure Service Bus, Hangfire, Quartz, Sidekiq, Celery, a database table). The years running it do.
- Can explain idempotency and "what happens if the process dies between these two writes" from a system they built.
- Integration work against outside vendors: REST or SOAP APIs, SFTP file drops, fixed-width or EDI files, vendors who change their output without warning.
- Owned production. They found out their job broke before the business did and changed the design so it could not repeat. A formal on-call rotation is evidence, not the requirement.Questions you will be asked:
- "Tell me about a system you built where the same job must never run twice at the same time. How did you stop it?"
- "Tell me about a production failure you owned where nothing errored and the data was just wrong or missing. What did you change afterward?"
- "What is the most TypeScript you have written?"The pitch to candidates
- Greenfield core of a real money system, with an architecture already written down and a CTO who will hand it over rather than hover.
- Small team, no service fleet, no twelve microservices, one database to search when something goes wrong.
- Every automated step earns trust on evidence (shadow, propose, auto). The engineer who builds that gets to decide how far it goes.
- Decisions are written. They will read the ones that exist and write the next ones.
- Texas based, remote within the state. No relocation.
- Billing is unglamorous and sticky. The agencies are the customer, the money is real, and the problems are concrete.Pay: $130,000.00 - $160,000.00 per yearWork Location: Remote

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Description

ASG is an unconventional group of market-leading SaaS software companies, serving industries ranging from behavioral health to transportation to childcare. ASG believes deeply in the power of people and data to grow great organizations, and that sharing knowledge, expertise, and resources across its community of businesses drives exponential growth. ASG has acquired over 50 businesses since its inception in August of 2016. We are backed by Alpine Investors and operated by world-class PeopleFirstTM leaders. Founders of leading SaaS companies continue to trust ASG to grow their businesses and build even stronger legacies for the future. To learn more, visit www.alpinesg.com.

We hire and unleash a diverse array of leaders across ASG whose will to win - and ability to do so with love - is the true magic behind our success.

Job Description

This role is a hands-on builder and enabler for ASG’s portfolio companies. The Senior Software Engineer will directly lead and contribute to software development projects across the full stack, using AI-native and agentic coding techniques to accelerate delivery of production-quality solutions. In parallel, this person will help train and upskill OpCo engineering teams through practical coaching, workshops, and real-world examples that drive adoption of AI-native development practices.
What You Will Do

- Lead high-impact build projects across ASG portfolio companies, partnering directly with operating companies to design, develop, and deliver software that opens new opportunities for the business.

- Work hands-on across the full stack, using AI-native development practices to accelerate delivery while maintaining high standards for production-quality code, architecture, and reliability.

- Serve as a technical leader and trusted advisor to engineering teams across the portfolio, influencing without direct authority and helping teams adopt more effective ways of working.

- Train and mentor engineers at operating companies on AI-native software development, sharing practical methods, workflows, and tooling that improve productivity and code quality.

- Design and host workshops, enablement sessions, and working labs to drive adoption of agentic coding practices across the portfolio.

- Help establish repeatable patterns, playbooks, and best practices that can scale across multiple companies, teams, and software environments.

- Collaborate closely with portfolio leadership, product stakeholders, and engineering teams to identify opportunities where AI-native development can meaningfully accelerate execution and create value.

Who You Are

- 7+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience building and shipping production-quality applications in senior or lead roles

- Strong software engineering fundamentals with a track record of building and shipping production-quality software

- Ability to work across the full stack, including infrastructure, backend, web, mobile, and databases

- Experience using best-in-class AI and agentic coding tools to accelerate software development

- Familiarity with tools that improve the SDLC, including AI code review, static analysis, testing, CI/CD, and observability

- Curiosity and discipline to stay current with the latest advancements in AI tools and agentic coding workflows

- Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to train and enable broad technical audiences

- Experience across multiple programming languages, frameworks, and tech stacks, with the ability to quickly learn new ones

- Sound judgment in code quality, architecture, security, performance, and maintainability

- Comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-paced environments and turning ideas into practical solutions

- Comfortable switching contexts quickly and operating effectively across multiple companies, teams, and priorities

Base Salary Range

The target salary range for this position is ($180,000-$200,000), and is part of a competitive total rewards package including an annual bonus, employer-paid benefits, L&D stipend and incentive pay for eligible roles. Individual pay may vary from the target range and is determined by a number of factors including experience, location, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. We review all employee pay and compensation programs annually at minimum to ensure competitive and fair pay.

A Secure Candidate Experience

All official emails and messages regarding opportunities at ASG, LLC, will come from our alpinesg.com email domain. Please be wary of communications from similar domains that may contain misspellings or slight variations. These could be attempts at phishing or impersonation. ASG will never ask you for sensitive personal information during the hiring process such as social security numbers, banking information or other personal details.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer: Ransomware Collections
jobs.description:
With 1,000+ intelligence professionals serving over 1,900 clients worldwide, Recorded Future is the world's most advanced, and largest, intelligence company!
We are seeking a Senior Engineer to help advance the next generation of our ransomware collection capabilities. This role will be responsible for improving the depth, reliability, and differentiation of our existing ransomware collections while expanding beyond traditional threat-actor sites into the broader ecosystem of infrastructure, identities, communities, and relationships surrounding ransomware activity.

The ideal candidate combines strong collection engineering experience with an understanding of how technical collection decisions translate into higher-confidence intelligence for analysts and customers. This engineer will work closely with our ransomware analyst and broader collections organization to ensure that our automated access strategy evolves alongside changes in the ransomware ecosystem.

A central objective of this role is to build collection capabilities that consistently provide intelligence beyond what is readily available through open-source ransomware monitoring.

What You'll Do:

- Own and improve engineering capabilities supporting ransomware collection, with an emphasis on reliability, coverage, timeliness, and intelligence value.

- Expand ransomware collection beyond leak sites and other conventional sources into user-focused approaches that provide greater visibility into relevant actors and communities.

- Partner closely with ransomware analysts to translate intelligence requirements and emerging investigative questions into scalable technical collection capabilities.

- Develop and continuously refine automated access strategies for ransomware-related sources, particularly where authentication, anti-automation controls, infrastructure changes, or other access challenges make collection difficult.

- Build infrastructure that enables the team to discover, access, monitor, and preserve difficult-to-collect ransomware intelligence at scale.

- Improve the resilience and maintainability of existing ransomware collection systems while reducing manual intervention and operational overhead.

- Establish engineering patterns that allow new ransomware sources and collection methodologies to move efficiently and reliably from experimentation into production.

- Collaborate across engineering, collections, and analysis teams to ensure collected data is structured and delivered in ways that maximize downstream intelligence value.

- Contribute technical leadership and mentorship within the collections organization, helping establish engineering standards and long-term architectural direction.

Technology & Engineering Environment:

Our collection systems operate across cloud infrastructure, distributed collection services, browser automation, and specialized network environments. Candidates do not need experience with every technology but should be comfortable learning and operating across the type of stack that includes:

- Languages: Python, Go, JavaScript/TypeScript

- Cloud & Infrastructure: AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

- Data & Storage: S3, PostgreSQL, Redis and distributed caching/storage systems

- Collection & Automation: HTTP-based collectors, browser automation, headless browsers, Playwright/Selenium-style tooling, authenticated session management

- Network & Access: TOR, proxies, SOCKS, VPNs, distributed egress and specialized collection infrastructure

- Messaging & Processing: Queue- and event-driven processing architectures

- Engineering: GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, observability and production monitoring

- Security & Intelligence: Dark-web and restricted-source collection, ransomware infrastructure, identity and entity resolution, and adversarial web environments

Experience building reliable systems against unstable or intentionally difficult-to-automate sources is particularly valuable.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means that our ransomware collection capability becomes increasingly difficult to replicate through open-source monitoring alone. Analysts should have earlier access to relevant information, greater context surrounding threat-actor claims, and stronger evidence for understanding relationships between actors, infrastructure, identities, and ransomware operations. The engineer in this role should also materially improve our ability to adapt as ransomware actors change platforms, access controls, infrastructure, and operating practices. They will turn what would otherwise be recurring collection problems into durable engineering capabilities.

This position may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and medical, dental, vision, life insurance and 401K.
