NOTE: Although this position is in support of our US Government work, this role is located in Wiesbaden, Germany.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like “Why are we delaying so many flights?” or “How can we better identify instances of money laundering?” As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.

As an FDSE your responsibilities look similar to those of a startup CTO: you’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.

Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. You’ll learn how to unpack a problem and understand the costs and consequences of its solution. You’ll learn new technologies and languages, and even develop them yourself. You’ll work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop.
Our Principles

- Impact: We take on meaningful and challenging projects that change the world for the better.

- Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter.

- Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on site, to understand and solve their problems.

- Trust: We trust each other to effectively manage time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves.

- Growth: We encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge.

- Learning: We often face entirely novel problems where we need to pick up a lot of new knowledge and learn how to use it to make progress. We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers.
What We Value

- Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics.

- Experience with logistics, materiel, sustainment, aviation, or readiness analysis is a plus.

- Familiarity with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.

- Understanding of how technical decisions impact the user of what you’re building.

- Strong coder with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar.

- Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, and comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users.

- Demonstrated ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal supervision.

- Willingness and interest to travel as needed.
Requirements

- Active US Security Clearance at or above the Secret level.
Salary

The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.

Our benefits aim to promote health and wellbeing across all areas of Palantirians’ lives. We work to continuously improve our offerings and listen to our community as we design and update them. The list below details our available benefits and some of the perks that can be enjoyed as an employee of Palantir Technologies.

Benefits

- Employees (and their eligible dependents) can enroll in medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as voluntary life insurance

- Employees are automatically covered by Palantir’s basic life, AD&D and disability insurance

- Commuter benefits

- If hired to deploy via SOFA to Japan, you will be eligible for the standard new hire relocation benefit if you need to relocate > 50 miles for the job

- Support for home and host tax returns and tax equalization

- Take what you need paid time off, not accrual based

- 2 weeks paid time off built into the end of each year (subject to team and business needs)

- 10 paid holidays throughout the calendar year

- Supportive leave of absence program including time off for military service and medical events

- Paid leave for new parents and subsidized back-up care for all parents

- Fertility and family building benefits including but not limited to adoption, surrogacy, and preservation

- Stipend to help with expenses that come with a new child

- Employees can enroll in Palantir’s 401k plan

Life at Palantir

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.

In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the state in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.

If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer for all, including but not limited to Veterans and those with disabilities. Palantir is committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. About Us:
Trimble is a global technology company that connects the physical and digital worlds, transforming the ways work gets done. With relentless innovation in precise positioning, modeling and data analytics, Trimble enables essential industries including construction, geospatial and transportation. What Makes This Role Great:
As a Senior AI Agentic Software Engineer, you will operate as an
experienced full-stack engineer who independently owns the technical development, quality, and performance of complex engineering work using cutting-edge agentic AI tools. You'll work with broad autonomy on ambiguous problems, set technical direction for your area, and raise the bar for the engineers and agents around you. You will play a critical role in bringing strategic visions to life through secure and optimal architectures. You'll join the Payroll team for Trimble Financials, building a React micro-frontend
backed by an event-driven .NET payroll system.

Key Exciting Responsibilities:
- Agent Orchestration: Design, own, and continuously improve the pipelines through which AI development agents perform coding, documentation, and refactoring on secure, maintainable, approved platforms. Set the team's standards for supervising agent output, code quality, and version control, and
own the prompt libraries, agent skills, and evaluation datasets that keep agent workflows reliable.
- Architecture: Lead the design of modular, cost-aware architectures for scale and performance that agents can implement. Drive technical feasibility and security reviews early in the PDLC, ensure adherence to Platform standards (e.g., TID, EMS, Modus, File Service), and lead prototype design reviews that turn product requirements into execution plans. Author and review ADRs, and weigh in on architectural decisions that span multiple services or teams.
- Feature Delivery and Testing: Deliver complex, end-to-end features across frontend (e.g., UI, accessibility) and backend services (e.g., APIs, authentication, messaging, infrastructure) with minimal guidance. Own testing strategy and frameworks for your area, including unit, integration, and E2E tests with explicit coverage targets and automated, continuous testing.
- Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Mentor and coach other engineers on agentic development practices, code review, and system design. Lead code and design reviews, share reusable patterns across teams, and help less experienced engineers grow.
- Business Outcomes: Own applicable KPIs for your area, ensuring your work and your team's technical decisions are directly tied to business outcomes.
Trimble Financials · Payroll · Senior AI Agentic Software Engineer Page

Essential Skills & Experience:
- 
5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including shipping and supporting production systems.

Deep, hands-on experience using and managing AI coding agents, with a clear understanding of their strengths, limitations, and error tendencies, and the judgment to know when not to trust them.

- Advanced proficiency in prompt design, agentic programming, oversight, and assessment of AI-generated code, including building evaluation and guardrail practices for a team.
- 
Practices and advocates for ethical AI principles including privacy, explainability, transparency, and bias mitigation.
- 
Proven system architecture design skills and strong experience in modern full-stack development, including frontend frameworks, backend services, distributed/event-driven systems, and cloud infrastructure.
- 
Experience designing E2E test strategies and implementing E2E test suites.
- 
Track record of mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction beyond your own work.
- 
Demonstrates an entrepreneurial mindset and ownership for relevant outcomes.

Technical Stack:

Payroll Frontend:
- Framework: React 19 and TypeScript, delivered as a single-spa 6 micro-frontend within the Trimble
Financials platform shell
- Build & Tooling: Webpack 5, Babel, Node.js 24+, npm
- UI & Design System: Trimble Modus Web Components (React) and Modus Icons, CSS Modules, and a
shared Trimble Financials UI library
- Data & State: TanStack React Query, React Router 7, React Context, and a generated payroll TypeScript SDK for all backend access
- Internationalization: ICU message format (intl-messageformat) with Lokalise-managed translations
- Testing: Vitest with React Testing Library and happy-dom (100% coverage gate), MSW for API mocking, Playwright for cross-browser/device E2E tests
- Quality: ESLint and Prettier

Payroll Backend:
- Runtime: .NET 10, C#, and ASP.NET Core in a modular monolith (Admin, Process, and Feed hosts layered into managers, engines, and accessors)
- Service Communication: gRPC via MagicOnion and MessagePack, plus REST APIs documented with OpenAPI
- Data: PostgreSQL 16 with Marten as the document store and Npgsql, with versioned schema migrations
- Messaging & Events: MassTransit over RabbitMQ (including saga state machines), and Kafka with Avro and CloudEvents for event feeds
- Observability & Resilience: Serilog structured logging, OpenTelemetry, health checks, and Polly
- Security: JWT bearer authentication and Azure Identity / Entra ID
Trimble Financials · Payroll · Senior AI Agentic Software Engineer Page 2• Testing: xUnit v3, FakeItEasy, Shouldly, WireMock.Net, and container-based integration tests

Shared Infrastructure & Delivery:
- Cloud & Deployment: Azure, Docker, Kubernetes (AKS), and Helm
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions, including PR checks, automated TypeScript SDK generation, and deploy, release, and rollback pipelines; GitHub Packages for npm and NuGet
- Security & Compliance Scanning: Mend and Snyk (IaC)
- Work Management: Azure DevOps Boards
- AI Tooling: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor, with shared agent skills, MCP servers, and agent-driven story-to-done and code-review workflows

Location: Lake Oswego, OR (Onsite four days per week)

Why You'll Love Working With Us:
At Trimble, we're not just a company that "does good"—we are a team dedicated to making a tangible, positive Real-World Impact. We build innovative solutions designed to solve the world's most critical challenges. From construction sites to transportation hubs, our work tangibly improves how people live, build, move, and grow.

Your Health, Your Wealth, Your Life

jobs.description:
About the Team

Help us build the world's most reliable, on-demand logistics engine for last-mile delivery! We're bringing on experienced engineers to help us create and maintain a 24x7, no downtime, global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash's three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced engineers to join the Traffic team and help build the next generation of DoorDash's Traffic platform. Our team develops and operates the critical traffic infrastructure that powers communication between thousands of services across multiple regions, as well as the ingress systems that handle external traffic entering the DoorDash platform.

You will work on core components of our traffic stack, including the Envoy Data Plane, xDS control planes and proxyless architecture. This role sits at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, and large-scale infrastructure. This role includes designing, building, and maintaining systems that must operate reliably and efficiently across some of the most critical and latency-sensitive workloads at DoorDash.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the Traffic Team within the Infrastructure organization. This role is hybrid working from one of our engineering hubs based in the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle or New York

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Design and build large-scale distributed systems that are high RPS and latency sensitive

- Troubleshoot, debug, and fix issues that affect production and maintain our SLAs

- Work collaboratively with other platform and product engineers to deliver on feature requests and solve their problems

- Find ways to improve the team's productivity and operational capabilities through the use of automation, AI tools, and other avenues

- Participate in a shared on-call and support rotation and lead production investigations and incidents
We're excited about you because…

- You have 8+ years of experience as a software engineer in infrastructure, networking, or platform engineering.

- Experience with Programming Languages like Go, C++, Python or Rust

- Experience with AWS and Kubernetes

- Background working on and debugging high-QPS or latency-sensitive systems

- You are curious, independent, ambitious, and can find solutions and make progress in an ambiguous and challenging environment

- You have proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software
Bonus points if you…

- Experience with service mesh technologies such as Envoy, Istio or Linkerd

- Familiarity with xDS or control plane architectures

- Solid understanding of networking fundamentals like TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, Load Balancing

- Experience building RPC frameworks or client-side networking libraries

- Experience with AWS Networking Primitives like Load Balancers, Privatelink, etc.

- Experience with Infrastructure as Code tooling like Terraform

- Experience with Gitops delivery tooling such as ArgoCD, Helm, Atlantis.
About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.
Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

As a Senior Staff Engineer in HRSD, you set the technical direction for model-driven capability across the HR domain, the agentic and conversational experiences that interpret employee, manager, and HR agent intent, reason over profile, case, catalog, policy, and knowledge context, and act on the user's behalf. Your unit of ownership is the architecture, standards, and evaluation infrastructure that let multiple teams ship those experiences safely — not a single feature set.
This is not an ML research role; you do not train foundation models. It is also distinct from traditional full-stack staff work, where systems follow deterministic logic. Two things shape the job: much of the load-bearing logic lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, context, tool descriptions, guardrails — and must be engineered with the same discipline as code; and because behavior is probabilistic, correctness is established through evaluation at scale, not fixed assertions.
What You'll Own
AI architecture for the domain. How agents are decomposed and composed, where reasoning happens, how context is assembled and bounded, how tools are exposed, and how autonomy is delegated. Own the multi-release calls: model selection and migration, orchestration approach, build-versus-adopt, and the cost/latency/quality tradeoffs behind each.
The autonomy boundary. Decide as domain policy which HR actions an agent may take, which require a human decision point, and which no agent should attempt. Anything changing pay, employment status, restricted records, or employee-relations matters requires a human in the path by construction — build the mechanisms that make those constraints structural.
The shared instruction and tool description surface. HRSD ships as product; customers configure, extend, and override this surface on their own instances. Treat it as a versioned contract with upgrade-safe extension points, deprecation paths, and compatibility guarantees.
Evaluation as infrastructure. Own the golden datasets, multi-turn suites, judge calibration, CI gates, and drift detection that let teams change behavior safely. Extend coverage to HR-specific failure classes: access-boundary violations, cross-scope leakage, jurisdictional and policy-variant correctness.
Production quality and safety. Observability for containment, hallucination rate, tool-selection error, unsafe action, and injection vectors from user-supplied content entering agent context. Because HR conversation content is itself restricted, design diagnosis that works without exposing what was said.
AI-assisted engineering standards. Convert ambiguous problems into testable specs; define what accountable agent-assisted delivery looks like for the domain — specification standards, review expectations, verification harnesses — and hold the line on it.
Hands-on where it matters. The hard integration, the risky migration, the prototype that settles an architectural argument, the incident nobody else can unblock.
Partner across functions. Collaborate efficiently with product, engineering, design to co-create scalable AI solutions and translate business needs into robust technical designs.

Qualifications

What You Bring:
7+ years of software engineering, with a record of technical direction adopted beyond your immediate team.
Direct, hands-on experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing autonomous workflows, and building the evaluation that verifies them.
Production experience with LLM APIs, retrieval-grounded features, agent orchestration, tool and function calling, and structured output enforcement — including at least one model or orchestration migration carried through production.
Entitlement-aware data handling: per-user access enforcement in retrieval and tool layers, scope separation between roles, and handling of restricted records under audit.
Evaluation experience used by engineers other than yourself: dataset curation, judge calibration, CI gating, drift detection.
Strong command of system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing across front-end, server-side, and relational data work with a high quality mindset.
Effective, accountable use of AI coding assistants and agents.
On-call and incident-command experience on customer-facing systems, including ownership of the systemic fixes that followed.
Experience in software stack including Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, React and demonstrated ability to quickly learn new tools and frameworks.
Bachelor's degree in CS, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred
HR domain depth: case management, employee journey and lifecycle, or payroll/benefits/leave/absence sufficient to set requirements.
Integration with core HR, payroll, or benefits systems of record, including reconciliation and eventual-consistency patterns.
Contribution in a Forward deployment model to champion customer adoption.

In this role, engineers spend approximately 60–75% of their time coding, working hands-on with code, data, and modern tools (including AI-assisted development, cloud services, and automation frameworks) to deliver secure, scalable, and high-quality technology solutions that drive business outcomes in the fintech sector. They collaborate with cross-functional teams – product managers, designers, data scientists, QA, operations, and compliance – to translate business requirements into robust technical solutions, all while adhering to best practices, security standards, and regulatory requirements.

Experience in technologies/software systems or a directly related field.

Preferred Qualifications:

6 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor's Degree or 4 or more years of relevant experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Master's, MBA, JD, MD) or up to 3 years of relevant experience with a PhD.
- 
Experience building high-volume, highly available, consumer- or client-facing platforms.
- 
Hands-on exposure to public cloud platforms and managed AI services.

Knowledge of model evaluation, hallucination mitigation, AI observability, token and infrastructure cost management, and privacy controls.

Experience mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction across multiple teams.

Technical Skills:

Java: Advanced proficiency in core Java, concurrency, collections, JVM fundamentals, performance tuning, and modern language features.

Backend Engineering: Strong experience with Spring Boot, Spring Framework, JPA/Hibernate, REST APIs, microservices, and distributed systems.

Data and Messaging: Experience with relational databases, SQL, NoSQL technologies, caching, and messaging platforms such as Kafka or NATS.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Staff Software Engineer, Records Platform
About Neumo
Neumo builds the cloud software that powers government. More than 4,500 state, local and federal agencies across North America run on our platforms, processing over 900 million transactions and collecting $44 billion in revenue for the communities they serve. When a county records a deed, a family orders a birth certificate, or a business files a local tax return, that transaction often runs through our systems.
That comes with a particular kind of engineering responsibility. Our platforms are systems of record for legally binding documents and public funds. Correctness is not negotiable, downtime has civic consequences, and the data we hold is expected to remain accurate and retrievable for decades.
Summary
The Staff Software Engineer is the technical lead for key projects on Neumo’s Records platform (Land Records, Vital Records and Search). County recorders and clerks use Records to record deeds, index documents, issue certified birth, death and marriage certificates, and give the public secure access to records that go back generations. Every recorded document has legal weight, so correctness, security and reliability are essential.
Records is a key area of investment for Neumo. We are evolving it from a tightly coupled, manually configured platform that depends on specific peripherals into a best-in-class product that meets customers where they are. The Staff Engineer designs and builds scalable solutions, guides project-level technical decisions, and sets the technical standards the team works to. This role requires deep expertise in cloud-based micro service architecture and technology. It also requires leadership skills: influencing team decisions, championing quality and mentoring Senior Engineers, many of whom work alongside newer team members.
The Staff Engineer reports to a Software Engineering Manager on the Records platform. The manager leads people and delivery, and the Staff Engineer leads on technical depth and direction.
Duties and Responsibilities
- 
Serve as technical lead on key Records projects. Work with cross-functional teams to gather requirements, shape solutions and guide implementation from design through production.
- 
Design, build and maintain advanced features within the Records platform, such as eRecording and eSubmission, automated indexing, search, certified copy requests, property fraud alerts, and ID verification and payment integrations.
- 
Provide technical direction for the broader modernization. That includes decoupling tightly coupled components, replacing manual configuration with configurable, self-service setup, and removing dependencies on specific peripherals.
- 
Design for configurability across jurisdictions, so the platform fits each county’s statutes, workflows and level of digital maturity without custom code.
- 
Own the technical direction for Records search, including indexing strategy, relevance, query performance and scaling for large volumes of recorded documents.
- 
Design data migration approaches that move customers and their historical records onto the modern platform with full data accuracy and record integrity.
- 
Partner with Senior Engineers, product, architects and leadership to create, refine and document technical standards, including standards for search and related infrastructure.
- 
Write and maintain architecture decision records so the reasons behind key choices outlast any one person.
- 
Set the code review and quality bar for the team, including review standards and test strategies for AI-generated code under Neumo’s agentic delivery model.
- 
Help the team work well from approved specifications. Write precise specs, show how to direct AI agents effectively, and make sure engineers own what ships.
- 
Conduct thorough code reviews, troubleshoot complex issues, and resolve hard performance, reliability and data quality problems.
- 
Lead the technical response to serious production incidents, and make sure post-incident follow-up actually improves the platform.
- 
Contribute to CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, automated testing and observability to support reliable, repeatable releases.
- 
Mentor Senior Engineers on design, code quality and development standards, and help them grow into technical leaders.
- 
Reduce key-person risk by documenting platform knowledge and spreading expertise through pairing, design reviews and walkthroughs.
- 
Build on Neumo’s shared enterprise services, such as identity and access, payments, notifications, reporting and search, instead of rebuilding them within Records. Partner with Platform Engineering where Records needs something new.
- 
Embed secure development practices, including vulnerability scanning, secrets management and access control, in line with the frameworks our government customers require.
- 
Stay current with emerging technologies in search, cloud and AI-assisted engineering. Run small, deliberate experiments and bring what works back to the team.
Qualifications
- 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- 
8+ years of experience in full-stack development and cloud software, across both Microsoft and open-source technology stacks.
- 
Advanced backend coding skills in Java and .NET, including both .NET Framework and modern .NET. Experience with Python or Node.js/TypeScript is a plus.
- 
Strong front-end experience with React, including building responsive, accessible user interfaces for both staff and public users.
- 
Deep experience designing, building and operating microservices, including service boundaries, API design and versioning, inter-service communication, and resilience patterns.
- 
Proficiency in Azure (preferred) or AWS and cloud-native design patterns, such as serverless and event-driven architecture, distributed caching and containerization. Examples include Azure Functions, Service Bus, Event Grid and AKS, or Lambda, EventBridge, SQS/SNS and ECS/EKS.
- 
Deep experience with SQL Server and other relational databases, and hands-on experience with document databases, ideally Azure DocumentDB (Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB). That includes data modeling, indexing and performance tuning, plus strong knowledge of cloud storage and data management best practices.
- 
Strong expertise in search platforms such as Elasticsearch, Azure AI Search, OpenSearch, Solr or Lucene, and experience optimizing large-scale search architectures.
- 
A track record of leading the modernization of tightly coupled or legacy systems into microservices, while keeping them stable in production.
- 
Experience with high-volume data processing and large-scale data migrations.
- 
Experience serving as a hands-on technical lead on complex projects, including writing design documents or architecture decision records.
- 
Hands-on experience with AI-assisted or agentic development, and a clear view of where it helps and where it produces work that’s hard to maintain.
- 
Experience working in Agile environments, with a collaborative approach to problem-solving and technical mentorship.
- 
Understanding of security and compliance standards, such as SOC 2 and PCI, and how they apply to engineering design.
- 
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical topics clearly and influence technical decisions.
Nice to Have
- 
Experience with land records, vital records, recording or county clerk systems.
- 
Experience with document management, imaging or scanning technologies.
- 
Experience integrating with hardware peripherals, or moving away from hardware-dependent designs.
- 
Experience with eRecording standards or submitter integrations.
- 
Experience with multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
- 
Experience with spec-driven development, context engineering, or building reusable agent skills and workflows (for example, Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot agents).
- 
Experience with public-sector security frameworks, such as StateRAMP/GovRAMP or FedRAMP.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 days. You understand the Records monolith: its main domains, where they’re tightly coupled, and which customers and workflows depend on each. You’ve mapped how the platform talks to printers, scanners and other peripherals today, and where those dependencies are hard-coded. You’ve walked through the current UI with staff and public users to see where the experience breaks down. You know where manual configuration slows down onboarding and support. You’ve built working relationships with your manager, product, architects and the engineers on the team, and you’ve seen the agentic delivery flow end to end.
By 60 days. You’ve proposed a domain-by-domain modernization plan that ranks domains by customer value, risk and coupling, and names the first domain to pull out of the monolith. You’ve written architecture decision records for the key patterns:
- 
Service boundaries and APIs.
- 
Data ownership. When to use specific databases.
- 
A peripheral abstraction layer. This lets the platform work with any standard printer or scanner rather than specific models.
- 
The modern React UI approach. Including a shared component library and accessibility standards.
You’ve also outlined the design for self-service configuration, so customers and implementation teams can set up workflows, fees and document types without engineering help. Code review and testing standards, including for AI-generated code, are documented and in use.
By 90 days. The first domain is being extracted from the monolith and is close to production, with data migration and rollback plans in place. A working proof of concept shows the platform using standard printer and scanner protocols on at least two device types it couldn’t use before. The first modern UI screens are built on the shared component library and validated with real users. Senior Engineers are leading parts of this work with your guidance, and the full modernization has a clear technical path.
By the end of year one.
- 
Domains. Several domains run as independent services, with a published roadmap for the rest of the monolith.
- 
Peripherals. The platform is peripheral-agnostic in production. New customers can use their existing printers and scanners without custom work, and hardware-related support tickets are going down.
- 
UI. Key staff and public workflows run on the modern UI, with measurably better usability, accessibility and task completion times.
- 
Self-service. Customers can configure common settings themselves, which shortens onboarding and reduces requests to engineering.
- 
Upgrade and search. The .NET upgrade is complete, and search performance and data migration quality have measurably improved.
- 
Team. Senior Engineers are visibly stronger technical leaders, and modernization standards are being used as the model across Records.
Neumo Summary
With the backing of four decades of public sector expertise and corporate capability, Neumo has successfully supported government services. Neumo was honored and recognized for four (4) consecutive years as a GovTech 100 Company representing the top 100 companies focused on making a difference in and selling to state and local government agencies across the United States.
Neumo is committed to helping communities thrive and brings a wealth of experience combined with innovation. Today, Neumo offers more administrative and financial support to government officials than any other organization. And with a responsive, client-focused approach, we foster partnerships that give our customers the certainty they need to accomplish more.
Neumo offers a competitive benefits and compensation package and are looking for team members who will thrive in our dynamic environment.
Neumo is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Selection for a position will be made without regard to race, religion, national origin, sex, political affiliation, marital status, non-disqualifying physical handicap, and age.

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Electronic Warfare (EW) team is seeking experienced generalist embedded software engineers to build out the software ecosystem supporting a next-generation electronic warfare platform. As an Embedded software engineer, you'll develop high-performance implementations of numerical algorithms, collaborate with digital systems engineers to enable maximum-performance interfaces between next-gen RF hardware and software, work with DSP and RFML engineers to rapidly deploy bleeding-edge capabilities to our customers, and collaborate with the wider software organization to deliver seamless integration of electronic warfare products with the Anduril Lattice system-of-systems suite. You will apply state-of-the-art software construction techniques to ensure the timely delivery of correct mission-critical code.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Develop cutting-edge hardware abstractions in collaboration with FPGA, DSP, and firmware engineers.

- Design tooling for rapidly deploying advanced DSP and RFML models to detect and defeat emerging threats.

- Implement high-performance numerical algorithms for RF data generation, analysis, and manipulation.

- Develop correct, high-reliability software for electronic warfare that integrates with the Anduril Lattice ecosystem.

- Utilize infrastructure providing deterministic builds and configuration management for deployment, guaranteeing software traceability and minimizing the maintenance burden of our products.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 10+ years professional experience in software engineering

- Experience with software-defined digital radio systems

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience working with typed functional programming languages (e.g. Haskell, OCaml, or Rust)

- Experience with software-defined digital radio systems

- Experience with high performance numerical algorithm development

- Experience with Linux kernel module development

- Experience writing software that interfaces with FPGAs and GPUs

- Experience with Nix/NixOS

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

- No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

- Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

- What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.

Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Engineering, AI Tooling & Enablement, this Staff Software Engineer will lead architecture and technical strategy for AI transformation. jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer, Records Platform (T3)
About Neumo
Neumo builds the cloud software that powers government. More than 4,500 state, local and federal agencies across North America run on our platforms, processing over 900 million transactions and collecting $44 billion in revenue for the communities they serve. When a county records a deed, a family orders a birth certificate, or a business files a local tax return, that transaction often runs through our systems.
That comes with a particular kind of engineering responsibility. Our platforms are systems of record for legally binding documents and public funds. Correctness is not negotiable, downtime has civic consequences, and the data we hold is expected to remain accurate and retrievable for decades.
Summary
The Senior Software Engineer designs, builds and maintains features for Neumo’s Records platform (Land Records, Vital Records and Search). County recorders and clerks use it to record deeds, index documents, issue certified birth, death and marriage certificates, and give the public secure access to records that go back generations. Every recorded document has legal weight, so correctness, security and reliability are essential.
Records is a key area of investment for Neumo. We are evolving it from a tightly coupled, manually configured platform that depends on specific peripherals into a best-in-class product that meets customers where they are. Positioned between the Software Engineer and Staff Engineer roles, the Senior Software Engineer owns features from design through production and makes sound technical decisions within their area. They raise code quality on the team and help newer engineers grow. This role requires strong skills in .NET, SQL Server and cloud technologies, plus the judgment to work effectively in Neumo’s AI-assisted, agentic delivery model.
The Senior Software Engineer reports to a Software Engineering Manager on the Records platform.
Duties and Responsibilities
- 
Design, build, test and maintain features within the Records platform, such as eRecording and eSubmission, automated indexing, search, certified copy requests, property fraud alerts, and ID verification and payment integrations.
- 
Contribute to platform modernization by decoupling tightly coupled components, replacing manual configuration with configurable, self-service setup, and reducing dependencies on specific peripherals.
- 
Take on meaningful parts of our modernization work, resolving compatibility issues and validating changes.
- 
Build self-service configurable features that support each jurisdiction’s statutes, workflows and level of digital maturity without custom code.
- 
Develop and tune search features, including indexing, relevance and query performance, for large volumes of recorded documents.
- 
Support customer migrations by building and testing data migration tooling, with a focus on data accuracy and record integrity.
- 
Work from approved specifications in Neumo’s agentic delivery model. Use AI agents to draft code and tests, then review, correct and own what ships.
- 
Conduct thorough code reviews, including reviews of AI-generated code, and hold a high bar for correctness, maintainability and test coverage.
- 
Troubleshoot and resolve complex production issues related to performance, reliability and data quality, and take part in on-call rotations and post-incident reviews.
- 
Contribute to CI/CD pipelines, automated testing and monitoring to support reliable, repeatable releases.
- 
Participate in sprint planning and backlog refinement. Give realistic estimates and raise risks early.
- 
Document key design decisions and platform knowledge, and share expertise through pairing and walkthroughs so critical knowledge doesn’t live with one person.
- 
Mentor Software Engineers and newer team members on coding practices, debugging, testing and how the Records platform works.
- 
Partner with product managers, QA, architects, Staff and Principal Engineers, and implementation teams to clarify requirements and keep designs consistent with Neumo’s platform direction.
- 
Build on Neumo’s shared enterprise services, such as identity and access, payments, notifications, reporting and search, instead of rebuilding them within Records.
- 
Follow secure development practices, including vulnerability scanning, secrets management and access control, in line with the frameworks our government customers require.
Qualifications
- 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- 
5+ years of experience in full-stack development and cloud software, with a focus on Microsoft technologies.
- 
Advanced coding skills in .NET, including both .NET Framework and modern .NET. Experience with Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Java and React is a plus.
- 
Strong experience with SQL Server, plus working knowledge of NoSQL databases, cloud storage and data management best practices.
- 
Experience with Azure or AWS and cloud-native design patterns, such as microservices, serverless architecture, distributed caching and containerization.
- 
Hands-on experience with search platforms such as Elasticsearch, Solr or Lucene, including indexing and performance tuning.
- 
Experience upgrading or modernizing legacy applications while keeping them stable in production.
- 
Experience with high-volume data processing and data migrations.
- 
Experience using AI-assisted development tools, and the judgment to review generated code critically.
- 
Experience working in Agile environments, with a collaborative approach to problem-solving and mentoring.
- 
Understanding of security and compliance standards, such as SOC 2 and PCI, and how they apply to engineering design.
- 
Clear communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues and trade-offs to engineers, product partners and leadership.
Nice to Have
- 
Experience with land records, vital records, recording or county clerk systems.
- 
Experience with document management, OCR, imaging or scanning technologies.
- 
Experience integrating with hardware peripherals, or moving away from hardware-dependent designs.
- 
Experience with eRecording standards or submitter integrations.
- 
Experience with multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
- 
Experience with spec-driven development or agentic coding tools, such as Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot agents.
- 
Experience with public-sector security frameworks, such as StateRAMP/GovRAMP or FedRAMP.
Neumo Summary
With the backing of four decades of public sector expertise and corporate capability, Neumo has successfully supported government services. Neumo was honored and recognized for four (4) consecutive years as a GovTech 100 Company representing the top 100 companies focused on making a difference in and selling to state and local government agencies across the United States.
Neumo is committed to helping communities thrive and brings a wealth of experience combined with innovation. Today, Neumo offers more administrative and financial support to government officials than any other organization. And with a responsive, client-focused approach, we foster partnerships that give our customers the certainty they need to accomplish more.
Neumo offers a competitive benefits and compensation package and are looking for team members who will thrive in our dynamic environment.
Neumo is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Selection for a position will be made without regard to race, religion, national origin, sex, political affiliation, marital status, non-disqualifying physical handicap, and age.

Ready to be a Titan?
ServiceTitan is building the Developer Platform for enterprise-scale SaaS. DevEx is a newly formed, lean, highly agile team (3–4 people) building AI-enabled platform infrastructure — pioneering AI-assisted development tools and coding agent runtimes (like Codex) to help engineering teams operate at “AI speed.”

This is a Staff Software Engineer role per ServiceTitan's engineering leveling framework: 10+ years of experience, Advanced Engineer level, working across squad(s)-scale, large or potentially distributed systems.

What You'll Build
- 
AI-Native Tooling: Components of the agent orchestration layer and harness that let coding agents operate reliably inside ServiceTitan's systems.
- 
Environments: CDEs, on-demand provisioning, mocking, and data seeding.
- 
Build & CI/CD: Build parallelization, remote caching, test-splitting, secure and progressive rollout pipelines.
- 
Developer Portal: Golden Paths, scaffolding, and service/API catalogs.
- 
Guardrails & Compliance: Automated linting, security scanning, and policy-as-code embedded in workflows.

What You'll Do
- 
Nature of Work: Make core architectural decisions and design systems within your area; lead investigations and guide deep-level refactoring; demonstrate knowledge across multiple domains (agent runtimes, build infra, environments) and know how to glue distributed systems together.
- 
Delivery: Write code and set the standard others emulate — full rigor on testing for scale, resiliency, performance, and security. Roadmap large tracks of work with reliable estimates and help the team hit its commitments.
- 
Independence & Decision Making: Make technical decisions across a large area of the platform and resolve in-depth needs without needing to be told how.
- 
Ownership: Be the go-to SME for at least one major piece of the DevEx platform (e.g., the agent harness, or the CDE provisioning layer) — recognized by the team as the person who owns it.
- 
Leadership: Mentor engineers in technical design and architecture; participate in interviewing and hiring recommendations for the team.
- 
Partner with the Principal Engineer/EM to turn multi-quarter strategy into sequenced, shippable slices of infrastructure.

What You'll Bring
- 
10+ years of software engineering experience, with recent (last 6–12 months) hands-on platform or DevX work.
- 
Direct, hands-on experience with AI/agent tooling beyond process automation or code-review assistance — this is the line that separates a real Staff-level DevEx candidate from a strong platform generalist. Concretely, we're looking for: a primary dev environment built around a coding-agent app (e.g., Codex, Claude Code) that you run on both desktop and mobile, agent sessions you keep running continuously rather than one-off, and the ability to speak in depth about orchestrating more than one agent against real work — not just occasional prompt engineering or asking an agent to draft a spec from a brief.

Experience shipping CI/CD pipelines, build systems, internal developer portals, or test automation platforms in production, at a scope consistent with “large, potentially distributed systems.”

Practical fluency with containerization/orchestration (Kubernetes/Docker) and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).

Comfort operating independently on a small team — you're expected to see and plan around disruptions, not just react to them.

Preferred Experience

Some direct exposure to coding-agent-runtime work, even partial — the strongest differentiator against other Staff-level platform candidates.
- 
Experience where AI-agent adoption was a team or org push you helped drive, not just something you did solo — and where the work is current (roughly the last 3 months), not a project you haven't touched in over a year.

Experience with compliance-sensitive workflows, change management systems, or policy engines.

Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

jobs.description:
Overview
Mainspring Energy is seeking a highly skilled Sr. Staff Controls Software Engineer to architect, develop, and deploy industrial-grade Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI) and SCADA systems for our Linear Generator sites. As a senior individual contributor and technical lead, you will define the architecture for modernizing our operator interfaces using Ignition, building scalable, site-agnostic UI frameworks, and implementing robust industrial communication pipelines using OPC UA, Modbus, and related protocols. You will bridge hardware controls, site telemetry, and operator visualization to deliver intuitive, reliable, and secure control interfaces across commercial, microgrid, and utility-scale deployments.
Responsibilities

- Ignition HMI Development: Lead the design, architecture, and deployment of commercial-grade operator interfaces standardized on the Ignition SCADA platform.

- Site-Agnostic UI Architecture: Build dynamic, site-agnostic HMI screens and tag structures that seamlessly scale across diverse power plant configurations, skids, and high generator counts.

- Protocol & Telemetry Integration: Implement robust communication interfaces and telemetry pipelines utilizing OPC-UA, Modbus, and SunSpec for real-time SCADA data exposure and third-party integration.

- Alarming & Diagnostics: Develop comprehensive alarm management, system of events logging, and diagnostic dashboards for deep visibility into site hardware and network status.

- Testing & Validation: Own the testing lifecycle for new features, including unit testing, integration testing, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation to ensure site safety logic and grid compliance.

- DER Integration: Implement strategies for integrating Mainspring technology into Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS) and complex microgrid environments.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with Product, Controls and Hardware teams to translate utility requirements and interconnection standards into functional software specifications.
Qualifications

- Industry Experience: 12+ years of hands-on experience in commercial power generation, industrial automation, manufacturing or utility-scale energy projects.

- HMI & SCADA Expertise: Deep hands-on experience building complex industrial HMI/SCADA systems, with demonstrated mastery of the Ignition platform (Perspective/Vision modules, UDTs, Tag Historian) and industrial communication protocols, specifically OPC-UA, Modbus TCP/RTU, and SunSpec, alongside relational database integration (e.g., PostgreSQL).

- Software Architecture & Scalability: Proven experience defining industrial software architecture, leading technical decisions, and delivering reusable, site-agnostic HMI/SCADA platforms from design through deployment.

- Grid Interconnection Standards: Experience with grid interconnection standards (e.g., IEEE 1547, UL 1741).

- Cybersecurity Frameworks: Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks for industrial control systems (e.g., NERC CIP).

- Technical Communication: Ability to create clear technical documentation and system diagrams that bridge the gap between industrial hardware and modern software.
This position is onsite at our Menlo Park HQ. The salary will be adjusted to reflect local market conditions based on employee location as well as the experience of the employee. Along with base salary, Mainspring offers pre-IPO company equity through Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) + benefits.

jobs.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)
jobs.description:
About Virtru:

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We're setting data free so that you can intentionally share it with others, but without sacrificing security, privacy, or control.

We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. Through the Trusted Data Format (TDF) open standard, we're not just protecting data; we're creating a new paradigm where security enables sharing rather than preventing it.

Think of us as the Android of data protection: a robust platform with an open core that developers and partners can build upon, coupled with our own best-in-class applications that showcase what's possible when you reimagine security from the ground up.

Backed by Iconiq Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundry Capital, and Tiger Global, we're helping Fortune 500 companies and government agencies discover that true data security means having the freedom to share, collaborate, and innovate — without compromise.
Compensation: $190,000 - 250,000/year

Team & Position Details:

Virtru protects data wherever it travels, for customers ranging from commercial enterprises to the Department of Defense, the Intelligence Community, Law Enforcement, and Federal Civilian agencies. Many of these customers are deploying one of Virtru's product stack in their mission environments, and some of those environments have no path to the internet.

As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) in the Delivery Engineering organization, you'd be helping to build a founder team focused on making these deployments simple, easy, and fast. You'll be relentless in the pursuit of one-click deployability, automating the hard stuff to ensure that we make every deployment faster and more reliable than the last one. You'll build and maintain a compatibility matrix customers can self service without engineering support, build automation to test and validate releases for deployability before they ship rather than after, and architect and deliver observability and diagnostics a customer can run and act on without us in the room. We build the automation, packaging, and tooling that makes that true, and we turn what we learn on each customer into something every later customer reuses.

You'll work directly with deployment engineers and forward deployed engineers to identify needs and turn long run books and disparate bootstrap scripts into working software that solves their problems. You'll also interact with our product engineering teams to influence their roadmap to deliver critical infrastructure and platform capabilities that improve deployment reliability and repeatability. You will work alongside a Principal Software Development Engineer who owns Delivery Engineering's engineering standard and reusable-asset architecture. You own the delivery path built under it, and you will write the criteria a release has to meet before it can ship to a customer.

The impact of this role is company and product wide, heavily enabling our goals to scale Virtru, partner, and customer led deployments non-linearly without having to throw more humans at the problem. You'll be expected to come up with AI-native design patterns that will increase our velocity without compromising our high bar for quality and security. The right candidate is excited about working on a small, nimble, highly autonomous and empowered team where everyone is expected to make high judgement, high velocity decisions independently and with urgency. If you want a role where the connection between what you build and what the company achieves requires no explaining, this is one.

As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), your responsibilities will include:

- Own deployment automation for the Data Security Platform: how it is packaged, installed, upgraded, and validated in environments Virtru does not operate. You will author the criteria a release has to meet before it is allowed to ship to a customer, and you will be the recognized authority on whether a given environment is ready for one.

- Build the air-gapped delivery path end to end. Offline bundles, mirrored registries, signed artifacts with a software bill of materials, and an upgrade that completes with no egress, no shell access, and no telemetry coming back.

- Partner with QA to build the reproducible test fleet and deployment test harness that proves a release works across the Kubernetes distributions, identity providers, and version states our customers actually run, and that produces our published compatibility matrix as a by-product rather than as a document somebody maintains by hand.

Additional responsibilities include:

- Establish the infrastructure-as-code baseline for a standard deployment, so every deployment and upgrade starts from a known state.

- Instrument deployments so we can measure time to value, upgrade lag, first-time-right rate, and cost per deployment, and hand that telemetry to our Operations partners to support continuous improvement.

- Design for disconnected operation from the start. In classified and air-gapped environments automated telemetry may be difficult or prohibitive to collect, so every collector needs a mode where a human reviews a local file and releases it.

- Convert what we learn on each engagement into a reusable accelerator instead of another runbook.

- Partner with our Platform Engineering counterparts on the build and release pipeline. They own the pipeline and you will own the criteria it enforces on our behalf.

- Carry field findings into product decisions with a documented outcome, so the same class of deployment failure does not arrive a second time.

- Act as the technical authority on hard customer deployment escalations, and convert each one into an enduring asset such as automation, tooling, or a product ticket (i.e., not tribal knowledge).

- Set the technical bar for the engineers who join after you, and help us define what good looks like for this discipline across our organization and company.

- Mentor, coach, and develop more junior engineers while cultivating a DevOps first mentality across our organization and the company.

Skills that will help you thrive in this role:

- Top 3 must haves

- You have shipped software into environments you could not reach. Air-gapped, disconnected, or otherwise customer-controlled, with no egress and no shell access. You have personally built an offline install bundle and a working upgrade path.

- Have worked with Kubernetes across distributions. EKS, OpenShift, RKE2, k3s, or their equivalents, with real Helm packaging depth and a clear understanding of how the same application fails differently on each.

- You embrace Infrastructure as code and reproducible environments as a discipline. Terraform or OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Ansible, and the ability to stand up a fleet that reproduces a customer's specific combination of distribution, identity provider, and version state on demand.

- Nice to haves

- Argo CD or GitOps at scale.

- Windows Server, PowerShell, and MSI or MSIX packaging with code signing. Many of our customers' end-user environments are Windows-heavy and some of our policy enforcement points are deployed on Windows client endpoints. Preferred, not required.

- Go proficiency, which is what the Data Security Platform and OpenTDF are written in.

- Operational depth in Keycloak, OIDC, and SAML, and particularly in identity providers that are not Keycloak.

- Federal compliance and software supply-chain tooling: STIG and OpenSCAP, SBOM generation, artifact signing with Sigstore or an equivalent.

- Hands-on experience with Zarf, Hauler, oc-mirror, or troubleshoot.sh. We may adopt mature tooling in this space rather than rebuild it, so direct experience here moves you to the front of the line.

- Podman and systemd-based container deployment, for the customers who will never run Kubernetes.

- Familiarity with Zero Trust security architecture and concepts such as Policy Enforcement/Decision Points, cryptography, attribute-based access control (ABAC), and identity.

- Existing TS/SCI US security clearance or eligible to be submitted for one. Not required for this role, but nice to have.

- What are the dealbreakers?

- A career spent entirely inside infrastructure you controlled. If every system you have shipped runs in your own cloud account, this role may not be for you.

- Needing shell access and live dashboards to debug. In our hardest environments, a customer emails you a file and that coupled with a phone call may be the entire diagnostic surface.

- Enduring operational toil without automation. If your answer to recurring toil is a better runbook rather than software to automate it, this isn't a fit.

- Inability to earn trust and credibility with partners and customers. You may be the person who has to explain to a skeptical government security team why our install is safe, or to an internal VP of Engineering why we need to prioritize critical platform features. Those have to be conversations you are willing and excited to have.

Virtruvian qualities that will set you up for success:

- Thinking outside of the box to respectfully challenge your teammates and managers in the pursuit of excellence

- Strong sense of urgency with an action-oriented mindset

- Able to collaborate and adapt to shifting priorities as business needs evolve

- Comfortable with asynchronous communication including slack, email, zoom, etc.

Perks & Benefits:

At Virtru, we believe people do their best work when their wellbeing is put first. This is why we make your wellbeing our priority with a thoughtful and holistic program that encompasses Occupational, Mental, Social, Physical, and Environmental Wellness by offering benefits such as…

- A Flexible PTO policy — we strongly encourage you to take time off (in addition to 14 holidays) to ensure that you are getting the proper time needed to unplug and recharge.

- A $1,500 annual Learning & Development Stipend focused on providing you the resources to continually learn and professionally grow.

- Frequent company-sponsored team celebrations that provide ample opportunities to connect with teammates and be social!

- Access to an Employee Assistance Program

- Access to Headspace, a mental health app tailored to your specific needs.

- A flat 3% contribution to your retirement account

- A high degree of flexibility — Have an appointment, errand, or family emergency to take care of? Hop to it! We give you the time and space to take care of you and your own first.

In addition to wellbeing, Virtru places a strong emphasis on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Our DB&I Council is dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace and making the psychological safety of each and every one of our teammates a top priority.

Additional perks include:

- Competitive compensation

- Generous parental, medical, and bereavement policies

- 401K contribution and stock options

- Full medical, dental, and vision benefits

- New Hire Swag and IT Welcome boxes

- Structured semi-annual 360° performance reviews

Virtru is committed to building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and everyone is encouraged to apply. Virtru is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, religion, disability, national origin, protected veteran status, age, or any other status protected by applicable national, federal, state, or local law.

About Matrix Systems and Technology inc

jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
The Observability team builds the platform every Affirm engineer relies on to understand the behavior and performance of our systems. Our platform ingests 200+ TB/day of metrics, logs, and traces from hundreds of services across 80+ Kubernetes clusters, and when a user's checkout fails, our data is how engineers find out why. Over the next year, we're moving to wide events, with one context-rich event per request, improving the signal-to-noise ratio to make debugging faster. We're also introducing log sampling and building observability best practices into agentic development and code review, so that AI-assisted code is well instrumented by default.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be the technical lead for Observability. You'll spend most of your time hands-on while defining the roadmap, driving cross-functional projects, mentoring a team of six engineers, and partnering closely with infrastructure and product teams.

What You'll Do

- You will own the architecture of Affirm's telemetry pipeline, balancing reliability, query performance, and cost at 200+ TB/day.
- You will design log sampling strategies that significantly reduce volume and cost without losing the signal engineers need during incidents.
- You will shape how observability fits into agentic development, so that AI coding agents and code review catch instrumentation gaps before code ships.
- You will be responsible for setting technical strategy for your team on a year-long time scale, and help your team tie it together with critical, business-impacting projects.
- You will collaborate across teams in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics to ensure technical sustainability, risks and trade-offs are well understood and managed.
- You will act as a force-multiplier for your team through your definition and advocacy of technical solutions and operational processes.
- You take ownership of your team's operations and availability by ensuring you have the right monitoring, triage rotations, playbooks, polcities, testing and alerting in place to support "keep the lights on" & on-call efforts.
- You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
- You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.

What We Look For

- You have 8+ years of experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.
- You have an extensive track record of developing highly available distributed systems using technologies like AWS, MySQL, Flink and Kubernetes.
- You have built or operated high-volume telemetry systems (metrics, logs, and/or traces) using technologies like OpenTelemetry, Kafka, and Terraform.
- You have a well-informed point of view on modern observability practices such as structured and wide events, sampling, cardinality management, and SLOs.
- You have driven adoption of a platform standard across many engineering teams, through both tooling and engagement.
- You have experience delivering major features, system components or deprecating existing functionality in a system through the definition of a technical and execution plan. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
- You thrive in ambiguity, and are comfortable moving from low level language idioms all the way to the architecture of large systems to understand how they work.

- You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
