jobs.title: Software Engineer III (Full-Stack)
jobs.description:
Sweet James Accident Attorneys is a rapidly growing, AI-powered personal injury firm based in Orange County, CA. In less than a decade, we've built a nationally recognized brand and a proprietary AI and automation stack that make us one of the largest and most efficient providers of legal services in the country. Our growth runs on a culture of excellence, compassion, and results: Our team is committed to exceptional client experience and to supporting one another in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. We invest in our people, encourage professional growth, and provide meaningful opportunities to build rewarding careers while making a real impact in our clients' lives.
Pay Scale: $165,000–$200,000 per year (base pay)

Work arrangement: On-site

Reports to: Chief Technology Officer

The Role

Build the apps and AI features our firm runs on, and set the bar for how we build them.

Technology is part of how we practice law. Systems we built and run ourselves read and sort more than 100,000 incoming documents and transcribe more than 100,000 calls every month, chase medical records, and put each case's full history in front of the people working it. We have replaced seven figures of vendor software with our own systems, and we keep adding more.

You are a senior full-stack engineer who builds with AI every day. You will design and ship the internal apps our staff work in, from the screen they click to the service and database behind it, and build AI into them where it saves real time. You lead projects end to end, review other engineers' work, and own what you build in production.

Responsibilities

- Build full-stack apps staff use all day. React and Next.js front ends, Node/TypeScript and Python services, and Postgres behind them: our records console, claims console, case assistant, review tools and dashboards.

- Put AI to work inside them. Pull facts out of medical records and police reports, search a case's full history, and run agents that do routine work for a person to approve.

- Connect the firm's systems. Salesforce/Litify, Outlook and SharePoint (Microsoft Graph), Zoom, Twilio and DocuSign.

- Lead projects end to end. Turn a request from attorneys or staff into a design, a plan and a shipped result, and measure whether people use it and how much time it saves.

- Raise the bar on quality. Code review, automated tests, and evaluation sets for every AI feature that measure facts captured, facts missed and wrong answers before a change ships.

- Run what you build. Deploy containerized services on Azure, monitor them, and fix them fast when they break.

- Grow the team. Mentor Software Engineers I and II, review their designs and code, and help hire.

- Protect client data. Least-privilege access, audit trails, and safe handling of medical records (HIPAA) and privileged case information.
Qualifications

Required

- 6+ years building production software, full-stack: React or Next.js on the front end, Node/TypeScript or Python on the back end.

- Production SQL and data modeling in Postgres.

- LLM-powered features shipped to real users: prompt and tool design, structured outputs, retrieval (RAG) and evaluation.

- Cloud deployment and operations: Docker, Azure or AWS, CI/CD, monitoring, and owning uptime.

- Experience leading projects and mentoring engineers.

- Clear writing: design docs, runbooks, and plain-language explanations for people who are not engineers.

- Sound judgment with sensitive data.

Preferred

- Anthropic Claude and OpenAI APIs at production scale; agent frameworks or the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

- Supabase and vector search with pgvector.

- Workflow automation platforms such as n8n.

- The Salesforce data model and APIs (Litify a plus).

- Voice AI and telephony (Retell, Twilio, Zoom).

- Legal, insurance or healthcare industry experience.
What Success Looks Like

- 90 days: You own one production app end to end, with tests, monitoring and a runbook.

- 6 months: You have led a project from design to daily use, and other engineers ship through your reviews.

- 12 months: Several workflows you built are part of staff's daily routine, with hours saved measured for each.
Our Stack

Python, TypeScript/Node, Next.js/React, Postgres and Supabase with pgvector, Anthropic Claude and OpenAI APIs, Azure Container Apps and Docker, n8n, MCP, Salesforce/Litify, Microsoft 365 and the Graph API, Zoom, Twilio, Retell, GitHub.

Benefits

- Benefits package: medical, dental, vision, and life insurance

- FSA or HSA option, depending on the selected medical plan

- 401(k) with 2% match after 90 days

- Paid time off (PTO) policy and paid holidays

- Ongoing mentorship, leadership support, and professional development and career advancement opportunities

In this role, you will lead the evolution of our multi-cloud SaaS control and data planes, manage high-density Kubernetes deployments across major hyperscalers, and partner directly with our AI Platform initiatives.

As a senior technical leader, you will balance greenfield architecture with hands-on systems programming and operational resilience. You will also allocate approximately 10–20% of your bandwidth toward high-priority Tier-3 operational escalations, identifying root causes in production distributed systems to inform durable platform architecture.

What You'll Do

- Architect Distributed SaaS Infrastructure: Design, implement, and scale multi-tenant Kubernetes operators, custom controllers, and orchestration workflows managing thousands of customer database clusters globally.

- Write Resilient Systems Code: Develop performant, fault-tolerant backend services and control planes using modern Go language & Python.

- Lead Cloud Networking Design: Own cross-cloud networking topology, ingress/egress controls, multi-region routing, VPC peering/PrivateLink topologies, DNS architectures, and service mesh performance (Envoy, Cilium, or Istio) across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

- Support AI Platform Capabilities: Collaborate across business units to build scalable compute, vector indexing pipelines, and ingestion infrastructure supporting real-time GenAI and vector workloads on Helios.

- Production Operations & Tier-3 Escalations: Dedicate 10–20% of your bandwidth to diagnosing complex production issues, acting as the final escalation point for deep infrastructure failures, performance bottlenecks, and kernel/networking anomalies.

- Security & Compliance by Design: Build infrastructure that upholds our strict enterprise compliance posture, maintaining automated controls for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS environments.

- Technical Force Multiplier: Author clear RFCs/architectural design records (ADRs), mentor senior engineers, lead cross-functional reviews, and partner with Product and SRE teams to align roadmap priorities.

- 8–12+ years of professional software engineering experience designing, deploying, and operating distributed enterprise SaaS platforms at scale.

- Deep Kubernetes Expertise: Hands-on mastery of Kubernetes internals, CRDs, custom controller development (client-go/controller-runtime), scheduling dynamics, and container networking/runtime internals.

- Strong OO / Systems Proficiency: Expert proficiency in Go and Python with an emphasis on concurrent programming, low-latency I/O, and distributed state management.

- Cloud Provider Networking: Deep operational literacy in cloud networking constructs (e.g., Transit Gateways, DirectConnect/ExpressRoute, Private Service Connect, CIDR subnetting, MTLS, and load balancing).

At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.
WHOOP is hiring a Staff Software Engineer to join the Business Systems team. In this role, you will play a crucial role in architecting, developing, and optimizing the backend infrastructure and user experiences that underpin WHOOP’s internal operations, enabling scale and efficiency across the organization. You’ll design, build and evolve critical services and integrations that support Supply & Demand Planning, Inventory Management, Order Management, Fulfillment & Logistics, Membership Services, and other business functions. This role is designed for a visionary backend engineer who is passionate about building scalable, reliable, and flexible systems, eager to tackle high-impact challenges, and committed to delivering user-centric solutions that pave the way for our growth.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
- 
Set technical direction for critical domains within the Business Systems team, establishing an architecture and roadmap that balances immediate business priorities with long-term reliability, flexibility, and scale.
- 
Architect, develop, and maintain backend services, APIs, integrations, and internal tools that connect business platforms, reduce manual work, and improve the accuracy and flow of data across systems.
- 
Design and implement well-loved user experiences to interact with backend systems.
- 
Partner with stakeholders across all of the teams mentioned above to understand critical workflows, identify opportunities for needle-moving improvement, and translate them into technical solutions.
- 
Lead engineering efforts for complex technical initiatives from discovery through production rollout, coordinating dependencies across teams and vendors and measuring outcomes through operational efficiency, reliability, and user adoption.
- 
Strengthen the security and resilience of business-critical systems through automated testing, observability, appropriate access controls, and improvements informed by production incidents.
- 
Mentor engineers and elevate technical decision-making through hands-on development, thoughtful design and code reviews, and clear documentation that builds shared understanding and ownership.
- 
Independently drive your agenda forward; this is a highly cross-functional role that needs broad trust and alignment in order to thrive. You must be skilled in driving this independently while also being able to move quickly.

QUALIFICATIONS:
- 
BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
- 
8+ years of professional backend software engineering experience.
- 
Experience delivering and operating production software for complex business workflows, with demonstrated technical leadership across multiple systems or teams.
- 
Ability to evaluate architectural tradeoffs across custom software and third-party platforms, considering business value, security, reliability, and ongoing maintenance.
- 
Deep expertise in designing APIs, working with relational databases, and integrating enterprise applications or cloud services, including managing data consistency, retries, and failure recovery.
- 
Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in at least one modern backend programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go, or similar)., with a track record of writing maintainable, well-tested code.
- 
Demonstrated ability to interface with multiple product domains, particularly in developing backend solutions for resilient, high-throughput data processing networks, task automation, and streamlined workflows to optimize business operations
- 
Deep experience with cloud-based infrastructure (e.g., AWS, GCP, or Azure) and distributed systems.
- 
A strategic problem-solver with the ability to turn ambiguous business needs into practical technical plans and communicate decisions clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
- 
A proactive, collaborative team player, eager to take on new challenges, continuously learn, and adapt in a fast-paced, data-informed environment
- 
Experience mentoring engineers and influencing cross-functional partners through collaboration, sound technical judgment, and a focus on shared outcomes.
- 
Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.
Learn more about our Software Org and how to be successful in your engineering career at WHOOP via our Career Framework.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

jobs.description:
Snap Inc is a technology company. We believe the camera presents the greatest opportunity to improve the way people live and communicate. Snap contributes to human progress by empowering people to express themselves, live in the moment, learn about the world, and have fun together.

The Company operates Snapchat , a visual messaging app that enhances your relationships with friends, family, and the world, and Specs Inc. , a wholly-owned subsidiary dedicated to making computing more human, in addition to Bitmoji , Saturn, and other digital services.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be the technical lead for the Spam & Abuse team at Snap!

Spam & Abuse protects the integrity of every Snapchat account. We keep spam, bot, and automated accounts off the platform, from the device and registration through everything those accounts do afterwards. We keep the rightful owner in control of their account by detecting and stopping account takeover and securing login, recovery, and sessions. We track how adversaries operate off-platform and turn that into live defenses. And we run the shared detection and enforcement platform that makes real-time decisions on accounts and publishes account risk that teams across Snap act on. Alongside this, our Secure Mobile Client team builds the client and backend mechanisms behind sensitive flows like registration, login, and recovery, as well as on-device safety surfaces such as in-app reporting and end-to-end encryption.

As the team's technical lead, you'll work across all of these areas. You'll set the technical vision and architecture for how we detect, decide, and enforce, make the hard calls on where to invest, and raise the bar for how the whole team builds and operates its systems.

What you'll do:

- Set the technical vision and multi-year architecture for Spam & Abuse, spanning spam and bot detection, account takeover defense, the detection and enforcement platform, and secure mobile client flows

- Lead the design of the team's most complex, cross-cutting systems, and review the designs of others to keep the architecture coherent across areas

- Drive technical strategy with engineering managers and product, and turn it into roadmaps that teams can execute against

- Mentor and grow engineers across the team, from new hires to senior engineers, and build a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and operational rigor

- Partner with engineering, product, data science, operations, policy, and legal teams across Snap to integrate account risk and enforcement into their surfaces

- Raise the reliability, latency, and quality bar of systems in the critical path for registration, login, and messaging, and lead technical response to major spam, abuse, and security incidents

- Stay ahead of how adversaries adapt, and make sure our defenses are designed to hold up when they do
Utilize AI tools to design and ship scalable services while upholding rigorous standards for code correctness, security, and production readiness

-

- Deep expertise in designing, building, and operating large-scale, low-latency distributed backend systems

- Strong understanding of spam, fraud, fake account, account takeover, or other adversarial abuse problems, and how to defend against them

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Sensing Systems
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

The Role:

We're hiring one of the first software engineers on our electro-optical team. Today that means long-range EO/IR sensors. In future it could mean sensors on mobile and airborne platforms. Wherever the sensor sits, the job is the software that makes it, and every sensor around it, act as one system.

This is a software engineering role first. You don't need to be a camera or computer vision specialist. You do need to be an excellent engineer who is curious about physical systems and understands how real sensors behave: they drift, they disagree with each other, and a field test doesn't care what the simulation said.

You'll join a small, elite team that takes its own work into the field. You'll test live, change code live, and see how it holds up on the next flight. The capabilities you build will push the frontier of what these systems can do, and few engineers anywhere get to work this close to the hardware, the mission and the result.

We're also changing how we build software. The aim is to take a feature or a new capability and develop as much of it as possible without real hardware, then push it up the chain: through simulation, through hardware in the loop, and on to full end-to-end tests in the real world. Simulation will keep improving, but real hardware will always have the final say. So we're building the harnesses and graphs that carry a capability through every one of those stages, with AI doing as much of the work as it can be trusted with. The end state is fully autonomous, end-to-end tests run against real hardware at our test sites. This is what you'll be building.

What You'll Build:

- Software that works on any sensor. Code that stays generic across many different camera heads and configurations while still hitting its performance bar, and flexes to whatever the mission and the customer demand.

- The path from desk to field. Harnesses and graphs that take a capability from first commit through simulation and hardware in the loop to a full end-to-end test, with as little manual effort as possible.

- Autonomous field testing. The system that runs complete tests against real hardware at our test sites on its own, and reports back what happened.

- Better simulation and replay. So more of every feature can be built and proven before it touches hardware.

- Multi-sensor integration. The interfaces, timing and data flow that let radar, cameras and other sensors work as one system.

- Fielded software. Deployment, monitoring and live fixes for systems running on edge hardware at test and customer sites.

This Role Is Not:

- Algorithm research. You'll build and ship software, not invent new detection or tracking algorithms.

- Physics modeling. You won't be building high-fidelity physics models in MATLAB or Simulink.

- Applied machine learning. You won't be training models on sensor data.

- Pure DevOps. You'll run infrastructure, but most of your time goes into writing software other engineers depend on.

What We're Looking For:

We care more about strong engineering fundamentals and curiosity than about any specific technology or domain.

- 8+ years of professional software engineering, including owning a production system end to end: you designed it, shipped it, and fixed it when it broke.

- A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or a related field, or equivalent experience.

- Strong Python. You build services and tools other engineers depend on, not just scripts and notebooks.

- Comfort with Linux, Docker, networking and CI. You can get a multi-service system running on hardware you've never touched before.

- Real leverage from AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, with a considered view on what to delegate to them and what not to. We treat them as a multiplier on skills you already have: you should be able to write, explain and debug your own code without them.

- Grounding in the physical world, whether from an engineering degree, hands-on work with hardware, sensors or robotics, or field time with systems that had to work outside the lab. You can read a schematic, understand a test rack, and talk to an optics or RF engineer.

- An appetite for field work. You want to be on site when your code runs, and you can debug and ship a fix before the next flight.

- A habit of measuring rather than guessing: you build the experiment, then trust the data.

Nice to Have:

- Cameras, EO/IR sensors, gimbals, radar, or video pipelines such as GStreamer or DeepStream.

- Embedded Linux or edge computing, especially NVIDIA Jetson, and GPU or CUDA work.

- Robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones or aerospace.

- Hardware-in-the-loop test rigs, or test automation against real hardware.

- Simulation or game-engine work (Gazebo, Isaac Sim, Unreal or similar).

- Building AI agent harnesses or workflow graphs.

- C++ or TypeScript.

- Defense or aerospace experience, or a current U.S. security clearance.

Location and Requirements:

- Work on-site in El Segundo, CA.

- Regular travel to test sites and field deployments.

- U.S. Person status is required, as this position requires access to U.S.-only data systems.

- Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Why CHAOS?

- Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

- Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

- Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

- Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

- Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Overview:

GitHub is shaping the future of software development in the age of AI agents — and search is at the heart of it.
As GitHub's lexical and semantic code search engine, Blackbird powers context retrieval for business-critical
experiences across the platform and our Copilot products, including Cloud Agent, Code Review, Copilot CLI, and VS Code.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help develop, scale, operate and extend Blackbird including integrating with AI Agents and developing new AI-powered software development workflows. You'll be part of our Copilot Agents organization, positively impacting millions of software developers and AI agents around the world who are building everything from open source to global enterprises.

We are looking for creative problem solvers and diverse thinkers, people who care about culture as well as customers and features. We believe that how we do things is as important as what we do. Big vision, a common purpose, passion for quality, curiosity, dedication, and investment in fun and collaboration are what lead to great results. Great products reflect the teams that build them.

More of the world’s development data lives on GitHub than anywhere else. Helping developers navigate and understand that data is a core part of GitHub’s mission, and an area with significant potential we have only begun to realize. We have high aspirations for how we can help developers understand and navigate code, and for making collaboration more seamless. The foundation for these efforts is our purpose-built code search engine which powers lexical and semantic code search in GitHub’s core search experience as well as GitHub’s Copilot products.

The ideal candidate has strong experience with distributed systems, search at scale, reliability engineering, and/or generative AI application architectures, as well as the ability to work autonomously, learn quickly, and communicate and set technical direction. You will be working within a strong team of staff and principal engineers as well as collaborate with partner teams across the Copilot Agents organization.

As a software engineer at GitHub, you will enhance the collaboration experience at GitHub by working closely with a community of engineers and designers with a distributed, diverse and passionate team delivering the services that millions of developers depend on. jobs.description:
About Tutor

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

The Role
We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to lead the design and implementation of core software systems across our stack. This role is less about writing isolated features and more about owning architecture, setting technical direction, and building scalable, reliable platforms that support machine learning, robotics, and operations at scale.

You will work across backend services, data and ML infrastructure, internal tools, and customer-facing systems, while collaborating closely with robotics, hardware, and operations teams. Robotics is part of the domain, but this role is primarily about building high-leverage software systems that make the entire company faster and more effective.
Requirements

- Strong programming ability and experience building large, production software systems.

- Proven track record of owning and evolving complex systems over time.

- Experience working across backend, infrastructure, and application layers.

- Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces and making pragmatic architectural tradeoffs.

- Clear communicator who can lead technical discussions and align teams.
Nice to haves (zero or more)

- Experience with Python, TypeScript, Go, or similar languages.

- Experience with ML platforms, data pipelines, or ML-adjacent infrastructure.

- Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, CI/CD, and developer tooling.

- Familiarity with robotics or hardware-integrated systems (not required).

- Startup experience or experience building systems from zero to production.
We're hiring at Senior or Staff level; the level is set by the interview. Senior: $180,000–$315,000. Staff: $240,000–$420,000.
Why Tutor?

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

Benefits

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

- Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.

- A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.

- Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.

- Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Deployment
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Every change to Anthropic's software has to reach production somehow: new code, runtime configuration, feature flags, infrastructure changes. Our team builds the systems those changes travel through. Our mission is to give every team at Anthropic a fast, safe, and predictable path from change to production.

We sit within Anthropic's Infrastructure organization and own pipelines, staged rollouts, health-gated promotion, and rollback, along with runtime configuration, feature flags, and the systems that deliver code and artifacts to machines across a very large fleet. You'll own a meaningful part of this end to end, from design through operating it in production.

If you want your work to shape how fast and how safely Anthropic ships, this could be a great fit.

Key responsibilities

- Set technical direction for major parts of the deployment platform and own them end to end: design, implementation, and operations

- Build rollout safety into the platform, including progressive delivery, health-gated promotion, automatic pause and rollback, and deploy controls that teams manage themselves

- Design APIs and abstractions that work equally well for engineers and for AI agents

- Extend the platform to new workload types and runtimes, from Kubernetes to serverless and edge platforms

- Build and operate runtime configuration and feature flag systems with validation, gradual rollout, and fast rollback

- Build infrastructure-as-code workflows that many teams rely on for safe, routine changes

- Scale artifact distribution so code and configuration reach machines quickly and efficiently

- Partner with Security so that the path to production is secure by default, with verifiable builds, least-privilege access, and auditable changes

- Work directly with teams across Anthropic to understand their deployment needs and bring their workloads onto the platform

- Take part in on-call and incident response, and turn what you learn into guardrails that prevent the same problem from recurring
Minimum qualifications

- Proficiency in at least one backend or systems programming language, such as Rust, Go, C++, or Java

- Experience leading the design, building, and operation of distributed systems or infrastructure in production, including technical direction across teams

- Experience with cloud infrastructure and containerized workloads, such as Kubernetes on AWS or GCP

- Strong written and verbal communication skills
Preferred qualifications

- Experience building deployment, release, or change management systems at large scale

- Experience with production on-call and incident response

- Experience with Rust in production

- Experience with progressive delivery and GitOps tooling, such as Argo CD or Argo Rollouts

- Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, including controllers and operators

- Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code systems at scale, including state management and locking

- Experience building feature flag, experimentation, or dynamic configuration systems

- Experience with artifact or package distribution, such as OCI registries, Nix, or content-addressed storage

- Experience with software supply chain security, such as signed build provenance

- Experience building high-throughput workflow engines or control planes backed by relational databases

- Experience building internal developer platforms and leading adoption across many teams

- Experience using AI agents in your own engineering work, or building systems that agents operate
Representative projects

- Build operator controls for progressive rollouts, including pause and resume that preserve rollout state

- Design a deployment engine built on fine-grained targets and their dependencies, so each change rolls out exactly where it needs to

- Build cluster-health-aware rollouts that steer around unhealthy clusters

- Add a new workload type to the platform, including its rollout, verification, and rollback behavior

- Design a deployment control plane that handles sharp bursts of agent-driven traffic

- Design a distribution system that delivers configuration and artifacts to every machine in the fleet as demand grows

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
Annual Salary:
$405,000 - $485,000 USD
Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description:
About Tutor

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

The Role
Are you tired of writing incremental code for massive CRUD web apps? Do you want to architect and build systems from the ground up that affect change in the physical world, not just the digital one? At Tutor, we are motivated by atoms not electrons: every line of code you write impacts the foundation of the global economy, solving the core technical challenges in robotics and automation at scale. Lever

As a Member of Technical Staff, you will lead design and implementation of critical robotics software across motion planning, real-time control, perception and optimization systems, tooling, and robot infrastructure. You will influence technical direction, mentor other engineers, drive system architecture across the stack from embedded to cloud, and champion best practices in software and robotics engineering.
Requirements

- Exceptional programming skills with deep experience across multiple languages and systems.

- Track record of designing and owning large, complex software systems.

- Experience leading technical projects and mentoring engineers.

- Comfortable working across the stack from low-level robot control to cloud services.

- Natural collaborator, strong communicator, and excited to solve hard problems that bridge software and robotics.
Nice to haves (zero or more)

- Proven experience with Python and prior experience programming robots (e.g. with ROS or other robotics frameworks)

- Experience with manipulation, motion planning, optimization, or perception.

- Experience with infra/dev tools (Docker, Kubernetes) and CI/CD.

- Background in hardware/software integration and real-time systems.

- Experience scaling robotics systems in production environments.
We're hiring at Senior or Staff level; the level is set by the interview. Senior: $180,000–$315,000. Staff: $240,000–$420,000.
Why Tutor?

Benefits

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Member of the Technical Staff, Product Software Engineer
jobs.normalizedTitle: Member of the Technical Staff, Product Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Tolmo
Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.
We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.
We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.
The role
Security tools have a reputation: dense, noisy, and built for specialists who tolerate them. We think that's a design failure, not a law of nature. As a Software Engineer on Product, you build the surfaces where people meet our agents, and you make them feel fast, clear, and trustworthy.
You'll own Mission Control, where teams watch a fleet of agents work in real time, and the findings workflows that take a validated vulnerability from "what is this?" to "fixed" in as few steps as possible. The work is full-stack: you'll shape the API and data model as much as the pixels, because a great interface usually starts with the right data underneath it.
You'll work directly with the founders, our designer, and customers, and you'll have real say in what we build, not just how.
What you'll do
- 
Mission Control: build the live view of agent activity, so people can see what an autonomous agent is doing, why, and how confident it is, without drowning in logs.
- 
Findings workflows: design and ship how findings are triaged, explained, assigned, and fixed, including blast radius, evidence, and the handoff to a coding agent.
- 
Full-stack ownership: take features from a rough idea through API design, data model, and UI to production, and follow them after launch.
- 
Craft and polish: sweat the details that make software feel good: speed, empty states, keyboard flows, copy, and the small interactions nobody asks for but everyone notices.
- 
Learn from customers: sit in on customer calls, watch people use the product, and turn friction into fixes within days.
- 
Raise the bar: help shape our design system, front-end architecture, and how the team thinks about product quality.
What we're looking for
- 
Taste. You can tell when something is off, explain why, and fix it. You have shipped products you're proud of, and you can show us.
- 
Strong full-stack engineering skills, with deep experience in TypeScript and React and comfort working on APIs and databases.
- 
A track record of owning product features end to end, from ambiguous problem to polished, shipped experience.
- 
Care for UX at every level: information architecture, interaction design, performance, and accessibility.
- 
Comfort with complex, data-heavy interfaces, and the judgment to make them simple without hiding what matters.
- 
You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and ship fast without letting quality slip.
Nice to have
- 
Experience building developer tools, security, infrastructure, or observability products.
- 
Experience designing interfaces for AI or agentic products, where trust and transparency matter.
- 
Design skills of your own: you're comfortable in Figma, or you prototype straight in code.
- 
Experience with real-time interfaces, graph visualization, or large data sets in the browser.
- 
Prior early-stage startup or founding-engineer experience.
Compensation & benefits
- 
Competitive salary, depending on level and experience.
- 
Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.
- 
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.
- 
Based in San Francisco; we work in person.
Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

jobs.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Enterprise Connectivity
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

A connected Claude is the difference between a general-purpose chatbot and a real coworker. We're building the connected enterprise on three fronts: zero-touch activation, a thriving connector ecosystem, and an enterprise control plane that lets organizations adopt with confidence. We own the path from discovering a connector to using it every day: default and suggested connectors, one-click setup, connector requests, and the identity and admin pieces that remove setup friction for a whole organization at once.

You'll be a technical leader who owns activation end to end, from the moment someone sees a connector to their first successful use of it. You'll also help to shape the foundations that help the connector ecosystem grow, and the governance controls that make it safe at enterprise scale. You'll partner closely with product, design and data science, and carry real ownership over what we ship next.

What you'll do

- Own connector activation end to end: measure the funnel from discovery to first use to habit, find the biggest drop-offs, and fix them

- Build and run experiments on default connectors, in-product suggestions, connector requests and onboarding flows

- Make setup close to zero-touch, building on open standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and the MCP authorization spec so one approval can turn a connector on for everyone

- Improve the connectors people reach for most, like Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, so the first experience works and keeps working

- Lay platform foundations for the connector ecosystem: reusable building blocks that make every new connector easier to launch, discover and activate

- Build out the enterprise control plane: admin controls and governance (domain restrictions, labels, permissions) that help security teams say yes faster instead of blocking rollout

- Partner with product, design, data science and sales to turn usage data and customer feedback into priorities

- Set technical direction and standards for the team, mentor other engineers, and lead with influence rather than authority
Minimum Qualifications

- Have shipped growth or activation work: onboarding flows, funnels, experimentation, and measuring what actually moves usage

- Are comfortable with authorization and identity (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SSO), enough to make setup flows simple without cutting corners

- Have built on large platform APIs (Microsoft Graph, Google Workspace or similar) and can debug failures on both sides of the boundary

- Have built platform or ecosystem surfaces that other teams or developers rely on, and care about durable, well-designed APIs

- Understand what enterprise admins and security teams need from policy, permissions and governance at scale

- Use data and user research to decide what to build, and can explain the tradeoffs to product and design partners

- Drive cross-team and cross-company alignment to ship, with influence over authority
Preferred Qualifications

- Have 8+ years of software engineering experience, ideally with 2+ years at a Staff or equivalent technical leadership level

- Contributed to or implemented emerging auth standards (IETF OAuth drafts, MCP authorization)

- Experience with data governance or information protection (sensitivity labels, DLP)

- Built admin consoles or policy engines for multi-tenant SaaS

- Run growth experiments on activation funnels

- Built AI products or agent tool integrations (MCP)

- Helped grow a developer or partner ecosystem around a platform

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
Annual Salary:
$405,000 - $485,000 USD
Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Join Our Team at RealWork

We’re RealWork, a team of builders and problem-solvers based in Austin, Texas. Our mission is to help home service professionals earn the trust they deserve online.

RealWork is the marketing engine behind thousands of contractors nationwide. We transform their best jobs into SEO-optimized stories, photos, and reviews that drive growth. Through integrations with leading field service platforms, we automate meaningful customer engagement after each job and use job content to help contractor’s online presence better reflect the quality of their work in the field.

RealWork is based 100% in the US and headquartered in Austin, TX.

The Role:
We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our small but growing engineering team. The ideal candidate will have demonstrable expertise in product development, data engineering, systems architecture and cloud infrastructure, with a particular focus on B2B solutions and an iterative, customer-centric approach. As a Staff Software Engineer you’ll lead feature-level implementation from scoping to delivery as either a solo IC or as lead engineer on a small pod of 2-3 engineers depending on the needs of the project. With the support of Product Managers, Designers, and Principal Engineers you’ll take PRDs, wireframes and technical design requirements for a feature-sized project, craft a project plan, set a timeline and refine requirements then follow through on implementation and delivery of that feature.

The Role of AI:
The elephant in the room. Every team is adopting AI and the conversation is inevitable. Here’s what to expect at RealWork. We view your human ability to solve problems, understand the technical ecosystem, take the lead, make cost/benefit tradeoffs and communicate with other humans as the real value markers of top-talent engineers - this was true before AI was a household term. The agent is good at researching, advising and typing. With that in mind we’ve developed a high-throughput, AI assisted, docs-as-code engineering framework we’ll train you in which means you’ll be delivering best-in-class, well tested, well documented features on a blazing fast cadence. Our Human-in-the-lead approach means you focus your time and energy on creative problem solving and the agent does the tedious work of maintaining thousands of lines of docs, code and tests.

The Product:
Our platform helps home service businesses get more business and operate more efficiently simply by doing their top-tier work. The platform marries data about customers, work done, photos, reviews, surveys and business reputation to create compelling stories the business can use to prove to new clients that they are better than the competition. The product is primarily a MERN stack with Typescript and AWS. We put an emphasis on keeping the codebase evergreen and focused on best practices while balancing stability and ease of use for the development team.

The Interview Process:
Tired of the 10-round interview gauntlet? So are we. We have a simple, straightforward interview process that takes less than 4 hours of your time - total. Sick of Take-Home Assessments and Algorithm Exercises before you ever get the chance to talk with someone? Us too. Let's get to the point, and see what we can build together.

Responsibilities & Requirements
- 
Demonstrated ability to work directly with stakeholders to define and refine technical requirements from a set of business goals or behavioral requirements.
- 
Ability to turn technical requirements into an iterative development plan with clear goals and timelines and then lead a small team to successful, on-time delivery.
- 
Demonstrate a mindset of operational excellence and full SDLC ownership - you’ll be responsible for ensuring not just feature delivery but a clear migration/rollout path, attention to observability tooling, metrics capture and monitoring and ownership of a successful launch after dev completion.
- 
Attention to DX - track record of increasing team velocity, removing development bottlenecks and automating processes to ensure top-tier delivery
- 
Conversational fluency in AWS best practices, enterprise software design patterns, and event-driven architecture
- 
Strong coding experience required - you’ll be hands on with the product. Professional experience building products with TypeScript, React, NodeJS and MongoDB is preferred.
- 
Practical application of AI developer tools in daily engineering tasks.
- 
8+ years experience building products in a startup environment is preferred
- 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science preferred
- 
Mobile experience in Expo/React Native or fully native apps, a bonus

Why Join RealWork?
- 
Startup environment within a stable, industry-leading company
- 
Competitive salary, bonus structure & equity
- 
Excellent Health, Dental, Vision and Parental Benefits
- 
Regular team outings & events
- 
Hybrid / Remote Flexibility
- 
Flexible PTO and Work Hours
- 
401(k)

We do not discriminate against qualified employees or applicants because of race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, sexual preference, sexual identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, and federal law or ordinance.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Work Truck Solutions is the operating system for the commercial vehicle industry. While the retail auto market is saturated with software, the $130B+ commercial truck market was operating in the dark—until we turned on the lights.

We are the only platform that connects the entire ecosystem: OEMs, upfitters, dealerships, and fleet buyers. By digitizing complex inventory data (chassis + upfits) and streamlining the supply chain, we don’t just help dealers sell trucks; we ensure American businesses get the mission-critical vehicles they need to work. We are a team of innovators, disruptors, and problem-solvers dedicated to one mission: removing the friction from the commercial vehicle industry. We are profitable, growing, and aggressively scaling our technology to remain the undisputed authority in this space.

The Role
This is a remote Staff Software Engineer role, our senior individual-contributor track, and the bar is high. A senior engineer is measured by the work they ship; a staff engineer is measured by what the team ships because of them. You are the person others look to when the problem is hard, the requirements are unclear, or the stakes are real. You set technical direction that reaches beyond a single team, choose the patterns others build on, and take the ambiguous, high-impact work that has no obvious owner and drive it to done.

Our engineering team is moving to an agentic way of working, where much of our code is written by AI agents under human review. You will help lead that shift. You know how to build and maintain the skills, agents and context that make AI agents useful on a real codebase, and you set the standards that keep what they produce correct, secure and maintainable. You define how the team builds with AI, not just which tools it uses.

This role is backend focused. You will spend most of your time in .NET and SQL Server, and you will know the frontend well enough to own a feature end to end. You will work day to day inside a software development team of 4-5 engineers, but your influence extends across teams. You make the engineers around you better through the standards you set, the reviews you give, and the way you teach. You have a bias toward action: you would rather ship something real, learn, and correct than debate an abstraction for a week.
Responsibilities
- 
Technical leadership across teams. Own the technical direction for your domain and influence it across teams. Make architecture decisions end to end, advocate for the better way to do things, and mentor engineers well beyond your own squad.
- 
Lead AI-driven development. Build and maintain the skills, agents, rules and context (such as MCP servers and the documentation agents read) that let the team build with AI. Use AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code or similar) to speed up delivery and to refactor and migrate code at scale.
- 
Set the standard for AI-generated code. Define how agent-written pull requests are reviewed and tested, including agentic testing, so that speed does not cost correctness, security or maintainability.
- 
Raise the team’s AI fluency. Teach engineers to work this way through pairing, code review and shared tooling. Evaluate new tools and measure whether they actually help.
- 
Drive the hard, ambiguous work. Take the projects that lack a clear owner or a clean spec, define the plan and the tradeoffs, and lead them to a shipped result.
- 
High-quality output. Build secure, scalable, high-performance applications with a strong focus on maintainability and clean architecture, and set the standard the team builds to.
- 
Lead through writing and specs. Write clear technical specifications to frame and lead a project. Establish the performance metrics for your domain, and make sure observability and reliability are designed in, not bolted on.
- 
Set and enforce quality. Own coding standards and lead peer code reviews. Use reviews and pairing to teach, not just to gate.
- 
Collaboration. Communicate clearly with a distributed team, surface issues early, and work fluently with both technical and non-technical partners.
What We’re Looking For
We are hiring a backend-focused engineer, and .NET is required. You must be expert in .NET (C#, .NET Core, ASP.NET Web API) and SQL Server, with a working foundation in frontend development.

Beyond that depth, we expect:
- 
A staff-level track record. Years of building and operating production systems, with a clear history of raising the bar on the teams you have been part of.
- 
AI development process experience (required). You know what skills and agents are, and you have built and maintained them for a real codebase and team. You can talk about that work in specifics: skills, agent configurations, rules or MCP integrations you wrote, how you kept them current as the code changed, and a time AI-generated code went wrong and how you caught it. You have a point of view on where these tools help, where they get in the way, and how to review what they produce.
- 
Full-stack range. Backend is your home, but you can own a feature from the database to the UI.
- 
Strong Git workflow. Branching, pull requests, and code reviews are second nature.
Backend Depth
This is the core of the role.
- 
Years of building and operating production-grade systems in .NET (C#, .NET Core, ASP.NET Web API).
- 
Demonstrated ownership of scalable, fault-tolerant, performance-critical systems.
- 
Strong experience designing API architectures (REST and/or GraphQL) with attention to versioning, maintainability, and real-world tradeoffs.
- 
Proven ability to handle complex system challenges, including:
- 
- 
Concurrency, data consistency, and race conditions.
- 
Caching strategies (Redis, in-memory) and invalidation.
- 
Asynchronous processing and queue-based architectures.
- 
Deep expertise in SQL Server:
- 
-

jobs.description:
Job Description
General Motors is reimagining automation at economy scale to make manufacturing more competitive in the USA.

You are a Staff Software Engineer who loves to drive physics-grade simulation. Modeling and validating manipulation, perception, SLAM, and navigation requires physics, sensor models, and dynamics that process simulators do not provide.

You will build the simulation infrastructure our robotics, physical AI, and test teams depend on, and own the roadmap toward virtual commissioning and digital twin capability. You have the taste to see important problems, the talent to build great solutions and the grit to get it done.

This role sits between core robotics development and the test organization and drives the validation that happens before hardware gets involved.

The Opportunity

- Build and own our simulation environment for manipulation, perception and navigation validation.

- Model robot platforms with physically accurate dynamics, kinematics, and actuation.

- Implement sensor models for RGB-D cameras, LiDAR and other supported sensors with realistic noise characteristics.

- Build scene and facility authoring tooling, including import paths from CAD and existing plant models.

- Integrate simulation into CI so scenario coverage runs on every release candidate.

- Support the AI team with simulation for data generation and policy evaluation.

- Drive the virtual commissioning and digital twin roadmap, including workcell import and collaborative authoring.
Quantify and document where simulation diverges from hardware, so results are used with a known confidence.

- 
The Job Requirements

Experience

- 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with 4+ years building or operating robotics simulation.

- Experience validating real robot behavior against simulation and closing the gap.
Experience supporting other teams as an infrastructure owner.

- 
Education

- M.S. degree or higher in Robotics, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related technical field.
Equivalent industry experience with demonstrated simulation depth can be considered.

- 
Core technical background

- Hands-on experience with a commercial or opensource simulator, including Process Simulate, Isaac Sim or Gazebo or comparable.

- Strong understanding of rigid body dynamics, contact modeling, and numerical integration, including where solvers break down.

- Experience with sensor simulation and rendering, including LiDAR and depth camera models.

- Experience with GPU-accelerated or parallel simulation for large-scale data generation.

- Experience with robot description formats: URDF, SDF, USD, and their conversion pitfalls.
Proficiency in C++ and Python.

- 
Systems mindset

- Ability to judge how much fidelity a given validation question requires.

- Willing to state when a simulation result should not be trusted.
Comfortable trading simulation speed against accuracy.

- 
Collaboration

- Ability to work effectively with remote teams across multiple time zones.
Treats simulation as a product with internal users.

- 
Nice to have

- Experience with simulation to real transfer and domain randomization.

- Experience with virtual commissioning or digital twin projects in manufacturing.

- Familiarity with Visual Components, Process Simulate, or comparable process simulation tools.
Prior open-source contributions to Gazebo, Isaac Sim, or the ROS ecosystem.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Developer Experience
jobs.description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose of economic empowerment. The blocks that form our foundational teams — People, Finance, Counsel, Hardware, Information Security, Platform Infrastructure Engineering, and more — provide support and guidance at the corporate level. They work across business groups and around the globe, spanning time zones and disciplines to develop inclusive People policies, forecast finances, give legal counsel, safeguard systems, nurture new initiatives, and more. Every challenge creates possibilities, and we need different perspectives to see them all. Bring yours to Block.
About the role
More and more of our engineering work now runs through autonomous agents, and those agents can only be as effective as the tools, context, and codebase around them. As a Developer Experience Engineer, you'll build the tooling and agent workflows that let humans and agents change our largest monorepos quickly and safely.
You'll own the interfaces engineers use to observe, steer, and give context to the agents working on our code. You'll also build the guardrails that keep complexity in check as those agents take on bigger changes. Large-scale work like framework upgrades, language migrations, and dependency health is still part of the job, but you'll do it by building and steering agents rather than making the changes by hand. This is a high-leverage role. Every improvement you ship multiplies across the whole engineering organization.
What you’ll do

- Build and ship the tools engineers and their agents use every day, such as CLIs, desktop integrations, and interfaces for observing, unblocking, and steering autonomous agents, and own their adoption, distribution, and support

- Design and evolve agentic loops (the plan, act, verify, and iterate cycles) and the harnesses, skills, and context that let agents do real engineering work reliably

- Build agent workflows that drive large-scale changes across the codebase, including framework upgrades, language migrations, and dependency updates, with minimal disruption to product teams

- Build the guardrails, tests, and automation that make large, agent-authored changes safe to land, and track the leading indicators of growing complexity

- Find friction in the development workflow for both humans and agents, and fix the root causes

- Partner with builders inside and outside of engineering to understand their pain points, and measure the adoption and impact of what you ship

- Set technical direction and mentor other engineers on agent design, tooling, and codebase health
What we’re looking for

jobs.description:

jobs.description:

We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to define the technical strategy for autonomous AI-driven enterprise operations at NVIDIA. You will set the architecture that transforms IT from manual, reactive workflows into agentic platforms operating at global scale. This is senior individual contributor role on the team: you will own the hardest technical problems, establish the standards that other engineering organizations adopt, and be accountable for architectural decisions whose consequences compound for years. Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills are vital for success.

What You’ll Be Doing:
As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you will define how NVIDIA builds and operates autonomous enterprise systems. Your influence will be measured in systems adopted, engineers elevated, and problems that stopped being problems.
Core responsibilities include:

- Own the technical strategy and reference architecture for agentic AI across enterprise IT : agent runtimes, tool interfaces, memory and context management, orchestration, evaluation harnesses, and safety guardrails and establish them as the standard that partner engineering organizations build on.

- Own the architecture of the integration and automation platform spanning ServiceNow, ERP and procurement systems, and endpoint-management platforms, including infrastructure, data pipelines, APIs, and user-facing applications and make the build/buy/deprecate calls that shape it for the next several years.

- Drive technical alignment across organizational boundaries, partner engineering teams, platform owners, security, and senior leadership resolving contested architectural decisions and building consensus without formal authority.

-
